explanation: L0/N1125- is a layer-0 token-identity key on the current BPE piece, not a semantic or topical detector: 97% of its variance is token identity and 2% position, 71% of integrated-gradient attribution sits on the peak token itself with only 19% on the token before, a piece's strength moves by a mean sd of 0.01 across four different preceding contexts, and nothing after the peak matters, so the pole is retrospective and context-free. It reaches the 0.25 x 0.351-scan-scale line (0.088) on a scattered inventory of ordinary free content-word pieces - ' commercials' 0.55, ' marketed' 0.52, ' meddling' 0.48, ' touted' 0.47, ' gardens' 0.42 (> ' garden' 0.13), ' lawsuits' 0.42, ' abroad' 0.41, ' domestically' 0.41, ' motive' 0.40, ' defendants' 0.35, ' second' 0.33, ' theft' 0.33, ' chemicals' 0.28, ' overseas' 0.28, ' command' 0.23, ' arguments' 0.21, ' buildings' 0.18 (> ' building' 0.02), ' lack' 0.18, ' involved' 0.13, ' crops' 0.13, and 0.4-0.8 on non-English content words (' yağ', ' présent', ' desde', ' sobre', ' sulla', ' Quando', ' devant', ' nombreux', ' لكن', ' 至于') and code identifiers ('NoSuch', '.commands', 'getStore', '.setColumn') - while it stays inert (<= 0.09, mostly < 0.04) on function words, punctuation and digits (' the' 0.04, ' a' 0.03, ' of', ' and', ' is', ' are' ~ 0.00), on the common core vocabulary (' cat', ' dog', ' house', ' year', ' time', ' government', ' development', ' business', ' importance' ~ 0.00) and on the Latinate derivational abstract-noun pieces that are this same unit's positive pole ('-ity' and '-ness': 0 of 461 and 0 of 102 pieces exceed 0.09 on this pole, while the positive pole reads +1.6 to +3.9 on ' complexity', ' reality', 'ITY' and +0.58 on ' ness'); membership is piece-level and scattered rather than semantic, so near-synonym minimal pairs decide it - ' second' 0.33 vs ' third' 0.00, ' motive' 0.40 vs ' reason' 0.00, ' command' 0.23 vs ' instruction' 0.00, ' chemicals' 0.28 vs ' substances' 0.00, ' commercials' 0.55 vs ' advert' 0.06.

N1270's negative pole is a layer-0 retrospective token-identity gate over one sparse, lexically specific band of the token-embedding space, not a topic detector: the strength is a fixed property of the token form (token identity explains 97% of scan variance, 85-93% of input attribution sits on the peak token, and a token gives the same strength in any sentence), only ~120 of the 9,433 token types seen at least three times reach the 0.30 active line, and the forms that fire are whole-word content tokens in five adjacent neighbourhoods of that band - religion/doctrine (' religion' 0.83, ' religious' 1.02, ' spiritual' 0.60, ' sacred' 0.75, ' faith' 0.42, ' worship' 0.31, ' Jewish' 0.43, ' Islamic' 0.34, ' Muslim' 0.42, ' Jerusalem' 0.33, ' priest' 0.33/' priests' 0.43, ' pilgr-' 0.40), sectarian and foreign-affairs names (' Syria' 0.67, ' Israel' 0.55, ' Palestinian' 0.39, ' Hezbollah' 0.87, ' Turkey' 0.39, ' Erdoğan' 0.31), nation and place names that are not among the handful used most (' Norway' 0.72, ' Ireland' 0.62, ' France' 0.41, ' Germany' 0.72, ' Russia' 0.31, ' Japan' 0.31, ' Sweden', ' Lithuania' 0.75, ' Greece' 0.34), occupational and institutional abstract nouns, mostly in their plural or long form (' profession' 0.74, ' graduates' 0.65, ' colleges' 0.57, ' faculty' 0.35, ' colleagues' 0.54, ' Congress' 0.67, ' Democrat' 0.33, ' credentials' 0.38, ' subscription' 0.44, ' deposit' 0.43, ' constituents'), and a thin technical/physiological set (' serotonin' 0.83, ' symptoms' 0.40, ' ultrasound' 0.32, ' encrypted' 0.41, ' encryption', ' prototype' 0.40, ' functionality' 0.39, ' myfile' 0.65, ' .js' 0.25), with capitalised Latin stem fragments such as ' Krak' 0.49, ' Wroc' and ' Tür' 0.38 also firing on their own; predict INACTIVE (0.00-0.25) for function words, digits and whitespace runs (which drive the opposite pole), for the everyday concrete core (' water', ' dog', ' book', ' tree', ' car', ' table', ' window', ' kitchen', ' food', ' night', ' mother', ' child'), for the highest-frequency personal names and countries (' John' 0.00, ' David' 0.00, ' Mary' 0.00, ' Michael', ' James', ' Robert', ' Thomas', ' William', ' India' 0.00, ' China' 0.06, ' Brazil' 0.01, ' America' 0.16, ' Canada' 0.04, ' Australia' 0.00, ' Africa' 0.00, ' Asia' 0.00), and for the three families the previous hypothesis over-reached on, which are withdrawn: clinical/medical vocabulary (' cortisol' 0.14, ' oncologist', ' biopsy' 0.19, ' diagnosis' 0.02, ' tumor' 0.04, ' dose' 0.09, ' vaccine', ' physician', ' patient' 0.00, ' surgery' 0.00, ' nurse' 0.01 - a clinical sentence peaks at 0.16-0.21), camelCase and library-style code identifiers plus ordinary programming words (' getUserToken', ' ApiClient', ' parseConfig', ' GroupLayout', ' routeProvider', ' instancetype', ' minOccurs', ' function' 0.01, ' return' 0.01, ' null' 0.00, ' object' 0.00, ' array' 0.01 - a code sentence peaks at 0.08), and diacritic/CJK word-forms as they tokenise in prose ('Kraków' gives Kr+ak+ów 0.08, '谢谢' 0.00, ' café' 0.12, ' Zürich', ' São' 0.00, ' señor', ' 한국'); predict inactive too for most same-field near-misses (' professor' 0.00, ' university' 0.00, ' school' 0.00, ' job' 0.04, ' career' 0.00, ' college' 0.03, ' charge' 0.11, ' business' 0.08, ' mosque' 0.09, ' temple' 0.01, ' church' 0.29, ' bishop' 0.09, ' God' 0.05, ' sin' 0.09, ' statute' 0.00, ' regulation' 0.11, ' audit' 0.00, ' invoice', ' portfolio' 0.00, ' insurance' 0.00, ' committee' 0.00, ' staff' 0.18, ' senator' 0.03, ' parliament', ' court' 0.00, ' hospital' 0.00, ' doctor' 0.02), so do not predict a new member of a field by analogy; outside these five neighbourhoods the active set is idiosyncratic and topic does not decide it (e.g. ' cave' 0.50, ' cloud' 0.42, ' desert' 0.43, ' recess' 0.50, ' crew' 0.37, ' thoughts' 0.40, ' mentioned' 0.40, ' questioned' 0.35, ' truth' 0.33 fire while their everyday neighbours do not). Structurally the firing condition is a SwiGLU conjunction - gate projection positive AND up projection negative - so a clinical word (' cortisol': g +0.14, u -1.20) or a code identifier (' getUser': g +0.05) is up-negative but gate-flat and misses the wedge that its field neighbours enter.

N2560's negative pole marks the end of a written quantity: it peaks when the current token is a short (at most 3 characters) alphabetic or unit-symbol fragment that cannot continue a hexadecimal numeral - any single letter g-z, or unit tokens such as ' m', 'mm', 'nm', 'km', 'h', '%', 'x', '×' - and the immediately preceding token ends in a digit ('The cable is 25 [[m]] long.' 1.55, 'rose 65[[%]]' 0.55, '#519[[m]]' 1.19, 'loc3[[g]]' 1.07); it fires much more weakly when the quantity is a spelled-out number ('twenty [[m]]' 0.67, 'twelve [[m]]' 0.44) and not at all after a non-quantifier ('the [[m]]' 0.00), so 90.8% of the 371 scan peaks at or above 0.25 x max sit on a token whose predecessor ends in a digit (13x the base rate, and 37x once the short non-hex-token condition is added). It is silent when the next token could continue the numeral or hex run (digits, and the hex letters a-f: '25 f' 0.00, '#519f' 0.00), when the preceding token is letter-final ('2s m' 0.31), and when the next token is a full word ('25 metres' 0.00, '65 percent' 0.06); its mirror-image positive pole fires on exactly those hex-letter fragments (a-f: 'fad', 'bbc', 'df') inside numeric/hex/ID strings, which multi-character abbreviations fire is token-specific (mm, nm, km, hr, min, mol do; ms, GB, MHz do not), and the residual 9% of scan peaks are unexplained word-internal continuation fragments ('acter', 'ycl', 'opol').

The positive pole is a retrospective unigram detector for a clustered family of relational/generic-vocabulary tokens: it fires on the current token when that token is a spatial or relational marker (around, through, within, behind, during), a temporal term (Friday, days, weeks, quarterly, today), a pronoun, number or light auxiliary (she, there, did, five), or a generic relational predicate (began, announced, gave, told, love, sits, runs, guide, support, range, interest, crowd), and stays near zero on semantically narrow concrete nouns (museum, pizza, river, senator, planet, banana) and specific action verbs (wrote, danced, scored, fell, raised). The same neuron's negative pole fires on exactly those concrete-specific tokens (princess, mat, fraud, Neil), confirming the generic-vs-specific distinction it encodes; the boundary is fuzzy (house/table drive it weakly, while time/always/get/every do not), reflecting an embedding-neighborhood detector rather than a crisp semantic class.

Fires on single tokens whose meaning is a concrete physical place or a region of one - terrain (valley, basin, canyon, gorge, cavern) and parts of the built environment (plaza, corridor, street, neighborhood, apartment, balcony, doorway, basement, courtyard, tunnel, depot, villa, elevator) - with Chinese place words (山谷, 城市, 街道, 村庄, 街区) firing as strongly, and graded within that class (measured in a fixed frame: valley 1.13 > plaza 1.01 > corridor 0.84 > canyon 0.66 > street 0.36 > village 0.29 on the scan max of 1.23). It is not a concrete-noun or written-register detector - institution/building words (school, hospital, church, market, bridge, station), ordinary objects and artistic roles (kitchen, table, chair, author, poet, painter) and abstract spatial nouns (place, area, site, zone) all sit at ~0 - so activity is predicted from place-of-space meaning in any language and any context, with three acknowledged offshoot clusters that also fire at 0.3-0.8: extent/position adjectives (spacious, cramped, ample, massive, interior, adjacent, opposite, coastal, urban, suburban), news/publishing role-and-outlet nouns (editor, reporter, columnist, newspaper, bureau, column) and quality adjectives used in property/procedure description (rundown, simple, straightforward).

N869+ is a retrospective, essentially context-free detector of the layer-0 token PIECE that spells 'code' (token identity explains r2=0.98 of its variance, position 0%; neighbouring text shifts it only about +-0.3). Activation saturates at 0.75-1.2 of max on the standalone word in any case and any attachment ('code', 'Code', 'CODE', ' code', ' Code', '\tcode', '.code', '-code', '/code', '_code', '(code', '[code'), reaches 0.75-0.85 on its plurals ('codes', ' codes', 'Codes'), 0.45-0.55 on 'coded' and ' coding', 0.28-0.75 on compounds ('bytecode', 'barcode', 'postcode', 'codec', 'getCode', 'encoding'), 0.25-0.80 on the word for 'code' in other scripts ('代码', 'コード', '코드', 'código', 'codigo', 'код', 'קוד', 'kode', ' kod'), and 0.25-0.40 on the bare continuation pieces '-ode'/'-odes'/'-oded' that BPE produces when it splits a longer word, whatever that word means ('nematodes', 'diodes', 'Explode', 'bode', 'brooded'); 'Credit'/'credit' (0.29-0.48 of max) is the only non-'code' family that clears the 25%-of-max line. It is INACTIVE (below 0.25 of max) on everything else: programming vocabulary that does not contain the string (python, java, html, sql, password, software, program, hacker <=0.20), on single tokens that merely contain the letters 'ode' (' model' 0.06, ' mode' 0.02, ' Unicode' 0.01, ' nodes' 0.00, ' episode' 0.01), on buried forms (' vscode' 0.17, 'urlencoded'->' encoded' 0.23), and on the graded near-misses ' encoded' (0.21), 'credits' (0.22), ' encode' (0.19) and ' decode'/' decoded' (0.13), which sit just under the line; 99.5% of the 20,858 token types in the scan never exceed 0.13 of max. Operationally: predict a window ACTIVE only if its strongest token piece is one of the 'code' spellings above (the letters 'code' inside a larger single token, as in unicode, node, decode or vscode, do not count), and predict it INACTIVE otherwise.

Fires when the current token completes a frequent local bigram or collocation (common function-word transitions like increased+by and at+the, adjective-noun or noun-noun collocations like young+princess and light+energy, and deterministic subword or digit completions like Mit+ochond and 1+0); activation level is set mainly by the current token but is boosted when the immediately preceding token is a strong associate, so swapping only the previous token reduces firing.

N2268- fires on the second token of a two-token unit that the preceding token has already committed to: a particle or preposition after an event/action word ('go about' 2.4, 'go over' 1.4, 'go around' 1.3, 'set up' 1.0, 'ready up' 1.1, 'plan up' 0.9, 'look about' 0.8), or the tail fragment of a word continued across two tokens ('Ke|isha' 1.1, 'Comp|iling' 0.7, 'Ans|ar' 0.6). Both tokens are required: the same particle after a determiner, pronoun or concrete noun is silent ('the up', 'hands up', 'table up', 'the word about' all ~0), the same verb with a particle outside the preferred set is near silent ('go back' 0.00, 'set out' 0.00, 'set aside' 0.00), and a non-event verb roughly quarters it ('put up' 0.37 vs 'set up' 1.16).

This pole is a retrospective unigram detector: activation strength is set primarily by the current token's embedding, firing moderately-to-strongly on a fixed idiosyncratic set of content tokens (' boils' ~0.36, ' door'/' stepped'/' range' ~0.24-0.26, ' cell'/' cat'/' password' ~0.07-0.19) while staying near zero on function words and on equally common matched nouns (' mat', ' dog', ' car', ' soup', ' table', ' house'). The one-to-two preceding tokens modulate the level by at most ~0.06 (less-constraining verbs slightly raise rather than lower it); tokens after the peak have no effect.

Predict active when the text names a place - a country, region, continent, city or nationality adjective (Germany, India, Japan, Europe, Berlin, British, African) anywhere earlier in the passage - and contains a national/institutional or civic content word (Federal, National, nation, America, US, Democratic, state, county, district, campus, college, hospital, restaurant, church); the peak lands on that word at 1.0-2.2, against 0.0-0.6 for the same sentence with a person, brand or generic location (Smith, Acme, the office, the venue) in the place slot. Words outside that class (table, car, money, water, peace, museum, market, factory) stay below 0.15 in every context tested, so a place name alone never fires the pole, and inside the class the place-free baseline is lowest for Federal, America, US, campus, college and hospital but reaches 0.6-0.9 for National, nation, restaurant, state and university in frames such as 'The committee mentioned the X during the meeting'.

This pole is a retrospective detector whose strong responses are confined to a memorized token set: the mid-sentence FALL forms fell/fall/falls/falling (fallen and synonyms like rose, dropped, collapsed stay near zero) and the capitalized pronouns She/He/They (lowercase she, and I/It, stay near zero), firing on the token itself in any frame. A subject-gated component additionally fires otherwise-silent past verbs (got/saw/knew/took) only after a firing pronoun subject, scaling with that subject's strength (got: 0.68 after She, 0.47 after He, 0.33 after They, 0 after I or in neutral frames); weaker context-dependent responses on determiners, complementizers and participles (the/that/stored/around) fall outside this claim.

This pole fires retrospectively on the current token when it is a content word (concrete noun, lexical verb, or a word-piece of one) filling a phrase-internal content slot, e.g. the head noun of a noun phrase ('sea level', 'the dog', 'your report') or a lexical verb after its subject ('river flooded'), and stays near-silent on function words (determiners, prepositions, conjunctions) in any slot. Within a fixed slot it is selective to a learned token subset rather than to the part of speech (dog but not wolf/chair, flooded but not danced, Ham but not plays), and the same token is gated by the preceding context ('table' fires after 'sea' but not after 'wrote' or 'on the').

Fires on the head noun of an indefinite noun phrase 'a/an (+ optional adjectives) NOUN' when that noun is an abstract, adverbial-idiom head (manner, way, fashion, basis, extent, level, minimum/maximum, glance, sense, attempt, while, time, rate, perspective, distance, hurry, whisper, percentage, degree; also 'friend'), as in 'in an efficient manner', 'on a daily basis', 'to a lesser extent', 'at a minimum', 'in an attempt'. The indefinite article is required: replacing 'a/an' with 'the', 'this', 'such a', 'my', 'no', 'any' or dropping it cuts activity to <=0.2 of max, and concrete nouns after 'a' (car, dog, house, table, room, project, idea, doctor) stay near 0; a preceding adjective (similar, lesser, timely, different) often fires moderately (0.4-0.6 of max) ahead of the noun.

This pole is a retrospective detector for the token that carries a time value in the text: the unit of an elapsed duration right after a quantity (minutes, min, mins, hours, h, seconds, strongest for sub-day units, reaching 1.8-2.2 of the 2.36 max), a clock or calendar instant (the ':' inside 17:48:35, the '–' of a date range such as August 17-20, 3:30 pm, 12 July 2021), and calendar or periodicity words used temporally (Saturday 1.08, Friday 0.89, July 0.70, weekend 0.69, weekly 0.66, duration 0.65, tonight 0.91 in a neutral carrier frame). It is not a general quantity, unit or token detector: the identical frame with a non-temporal unit (kilograms, metres, litres, volts, percent, mph, all 0.00-0.22) or with an ordinary noun (attempts 0.24, cats, people, shops) stays at the floor, 'minutes' in its record sense ('the minutes of the meeting', 0.27) stays at the floor, and the same nouns in an unrelated carrier are silent - with one admitted leftover I could not explain: a second family of computing identifiers (.Request, .Response, Command, requestType, .SelectCommand, query/SQL, execute) reaches 1.7-2.9 inside code-heavy text but only 0.0-0.6 in prose.

The pole fires on a frame-satisfying token: the current token is the specific filler that the preceding 1-3 tokens oblige (the '=' a WHERE condition requires, the 'not' that 'pleaded' selects, the 'to' that a 'from X' range requires, a non-final item in an opened enumeration, or the second half of a compound or collocation), with strength graded by how tightly the frame constrains that filler. Same-slot incongruent fillers go near zero while distant or non-constraining changes leave firing intact; zeroing the pole leaves next-token probabilities essentially unchanged (mean KL ~1e-5) and its Jacobian lens is flat (kurtosis 3.4, incoherent promoted set, 0% lens agreement), so it retrospectively detects frame satisfaction rather than predicting upcoming tokens.

This pole fires when the current token completes a locally licensed construction opened by a specific head within the previous ~3 tokens: a preposition or particle selected by its verb, adjective or noun (compared with, pleaded ... to, at least), a determiner or noun filling a transitive verb's object frame (flooded the, Add the, interest rates), a keyword closing a fixed code idiom (in range, zeros((, def add), or the expected continuation of an already-opened word or number chunk (Ham-let, Mitoch-ondria, 13, a.m.). The same surface token does not fire without its licensing head or after a head that cannot license it.

This pole fires on the token that completes a locally highly predictable 2-3-token collocation (common bigram or fixed phrase, subword completion, or conventional punctuation such as a dialogue-attribution comma), with strength scaling with how constrained the peak token is by the immediately preceding 1-3 tokens rather than by the peak token's identity or topic.

The pole fires retrospectively on the current token when it is a specific food or drink noun - cheese, wine, grapes, peaches, yoghurt, honey, jam, apples, oranges, eggs, fish, milk, rice, chocolate, cake, oil, sugar, lemon, lettuce, prunes, carrots, onions, tomatoes, cabbage, garlic, sausages - standing as a bare, undetermined item of an everyday eating, serving or recipe construction ('we ate bread and [[cheese]]' 0.99, 'the recipe calls for bread, [[cheese]], and wine' 1.11, 'we ate bread and [[grapes]]' 1.13, 'there was [[cheese]] on the table' 0.38), which is 0.4-1.3, i.e. 0.35-1.2 of the scan maximum. It stays at baseline when the same noun is determined or modified ('put the cheese on the table' 0.05, 'melt the cheese in a pan' -0.08, 'the cheese was fresh' 0.15, 'add the cheese and the wine to the pan' 0.10), when it is a generic staple rather than a specific item, even in the identical frame ('the recipe calls for butter' -0.03, 'we ate bread and butter' 0.16, and bread, meat, soup, salad, salt, pepper, flour, biscuits, lentils, steak all <= 0.20), and on ordinary narrative prose (<= 0.18).

This is the weak, near-floor counter-pole of a strong magnitude neuron: the same neuron's positive pole fires hard on measurable quantity ('times' 6.0, 'less' 4.3, 'more' 3.6, 'amount', 'many', 'big/large/long/short'), while this pole peaks on the word that carries a qualitative appraisal inside a comparison or improvement claim - above all the comparative quality word that closes a coordinated evaluation ('a safer and better world' 0.98, 'cleaner and better' 0.64, 'faster and better than' 0.54, 'more efficient than' 0.54, 'more fun, but easier on your body' 0.79, 'superior in energy efficiency' 0.43). It stays at the floor when that slot instead holds a measurable property ('larger' 0.00-0.09, 'longer' 0.00, 'faster' 0.03-0.12, 'bigger' 0.00-0.15, 'expensive' 0.00-0.05, 'cheaper' 0.00-0.18) and when the appraisal word stands alone without an evaluation frame ('a better world' 0.07, 'it was a better result' 0.00); it is retrospective and weak (its 0.98 max is the 12th percentile of layer-10 negative-pole maxima and 73% of scanned tokens fall below 0.033), with admitted leftovers on 'or'/'instead' and on final pieces of rare technical words ('orption' in adsorption 0.63, 'ability' in maneuverability 0.71).

The pole fires retrospectively on an approximator that supplies the value of an explicitly named measurement: 'about', 'around', 'roughly', 'approximately', 'nearly' or 'almost' directly before an amount, and 'or so' directly after one, when the clause names the measured attribute either as its subject ('the price/weight/distance/duration/delay/temperature/rate/probability/population/age/height/area/volume/speed is about ten ...') or as a measure verb ('costs', 'weighs', 'takes', 'lasts', 'measures', 'holds', 'covers', 'contains', 'reaches', 'earns', 'spends', 'paid', 'is worth' + about ten ...); the peak is on the approximator itself and is unaffected by the words that follow it. It stays near zero on the same words used in other roles -- topical 'about' and spatial 'around' ('talked about', 'walked around', 'The book is about ten dollars'), attributive measure phrases built on an adjective ('about thirty years old', 'about six feet tall', 'about ten metres long'), precise or boundary quantifiers inside the same measure frame ('exactly', 'precisely', 'at least', 'under', 'or more'), bare numbers, quantifiers of countable objects ('many people', 'several reasons', 'a couple of friends'), and plain intensifiers or frequency adverbs ('very', 'often', 'usually', 'generally', 'probably', 'relatively', 'particularly').

The pole fires on the head of a definite, particular noun phrase that names the passage's current subject matter and that the preceding ~100 tokens have made expected: 'your entire tooth' in a dental-advice article (1.06), 'the cumulative number' in an article about counting ants (0.99), 'his obligation' in an article about Jewish law (0.73), 'the following week' in a parenting post (0.70). Strength grows with the amount of on-topic context (0.60 with none -> 0.88 -> 1.11 after 3-4 dental sentences) and collapses when the passage is about something else or the same noun is indefinite or bare plural ('a tooth' 0.48, 'your entire teeth' 0.75, the identical sentence placed in an unrelated article 0.10); the word after the noun is irrelevant, so the pole is not preparing any particular next token.

The positive pole fires when the text refers to a specific-but-unnamed individual, or an indefinite subset, that is picked out of a plurality already live in the context, and it peaks on the determiner or quantifier that does the picking: partitives ('one of them', 'some of those', 'any one'), selection verbs taking a singular object ('select a partition' once the drive's partitions have been introduced, 'pick one', 'choose the second one'), and superlatives or ordinals that select one member ('the most serious', 'the first', 'which of the two'). It stays at the floor when the same word lacks that antecedent plurality ('You can just select a partition inside the drive.' alone: 0.21 vs 2.66 once a plural is introduced), when the phrase names a class rather than an instance ('it was one of the most serious': 0.14 vs 0.76 for 'the most serious happened'), and when the whole set is quantified or exactly counted ('all/each/both of them', 'two of them', 'three bicycles'), which drives the negative pole together with bare cardinal counts ('12 countries', 'eight rabbits').

The negative pole fires on the connector or degree word that carries a specification -- a preposition or definite article (' of', ' on', ' to', ' in', ' the'), a relative/complementizer pronoun, a degree or quantity word (' least', ' exactly', ' one'), or the head word that opens such a specification (' contain', ' stored', ' silent') -- when the clause read so far states the contents, attributes, requirements or status of a definite concrete entity (a password rule, a recipe's ingredients, a legal charge, a place's inventory, a formal fact). It stays at baseline for the same tokens in personal, imperative or ad-hoc sentences ('You need at least two hours', 'She has at least three cats', 'He depends on his parents') and in plain narration ('The cat sat on the mat': ' on' 0.09 there against 0.28 in 'landed on the Moon').

The negative pole fires where a clause is framed as someone's report, claim, guess or open question rather than as an asserted fact: it peaks on the complementizer ' that' after reportative or epistemic predicates ('reports that', 'claimed that', 'alleged that', 'suspects that', 'seems that', 'it is likely that'), on 'whether'/'if' introducing an embedded question, and on first-person hedges and direct questions ('I think', 'I guess', 'I'm assuming', 'at a guess', 'Do I...?', 'Is that...?'). The same connectives inside a factive or certain frame ('confirmed that', 'knew that', 'the fact that', 'it is clear that'), with a demonstrative 'that', and in plain declarative prose stay near baseline, while the opposite pole is the explanation direction: its output promotes cause and source words ('the reason', 'cause', 'culprit', 'origin', 'blame') and it fires on explicit explanation ('the reasons can be explained by', 'possible mechanisms for', 'what could account for').

The negative pole fires on the token that closes an insertion spliced into a running structure: the ')' (or '!)', '])', '),') that ends a parenthetical aside, the second '—'/'--' of a dash-bracketed aside, or the newline that ends an in-line comment spliced into a line of code — i.e. exactly the point where the interrupted clause, sentence or code line resumes (the resumption word right after the closer often carries a smaller echo of the same activation). It stays at the floor when the same words are written flat, for comma-delimited asides (4 to 10 times weaker), for parentheses that belong to the clause itself such as notation ('f(x)', 'sin(x)') or labels ('Fig. 4', 'Table 2'), and for code lines with no comment, while inside a real aside the amplitude is graded — largest when the inserted material carries a qualifying fact or number, smallest for a bare single-word label or adverb.

The pole fires when the text poses an open question that wants an answer - an interrogative clause, direct ('Is there a ...', 'How do I ...', 'Where is it?', 'What else should I ...') or embedded ('I would like to know where ...'), in English or another language ('Cuál es ...'), most strongly when the question is about a problem the writer is stuck on. It follows the question and not its surface tokens: it peaks over the question's opening auxiliaries or wh-word rather than at the '?', matter-of-fact questions with no problem behind them ('Is the sky blue?', 'Could you pass the salt?') and declarative paraphrases of the same content ('Is there a way to fix this?' 2.8 vs 'There is a way to fix this.' 0.8) stay low - except a 'way/solution to fix it' offered right after a described failure, which fires as hard as a question.

N380 is a formal-schooling unit: its pre-activation is a signed 'is this context about school and study' score, so the negative pole is exactly zero on schooling vocabulary and through clauses that are about schooling (school, university, college, campus, student, teacher, professor, faculty, lecture, exam, degree, tuition, classes, dropped out of school), and it goes negative everywhere else. The negative pole therefore fires once the text is off the schooling topic and grows with the distance from it - at or near zero (<=0.08) in schooling clauses and abstract academic prose, 0.04-0.28 in short everyday sentences, ~0.1-0.44 in encyclopedic/technical prose, 0.27-0.50 in narrative fiction, literary, markup or code text, and up to 0.80 on a single non-school word that breaks a schooling clause ('hospital' in 'She attended classes every morning at the hospital' reaches the pole's maximum, while 'university' in the same slot scores 0.00).

Retrospective detector of metatextual reference: the pole fires across a span that points at the text being written or read, at another written text, or at a named part of one - 'in this article / post / blog / chapter / section / page / report / guide / piece', 'This article will...', 'discussed in Chapter 7', 'see / refer to Section 3, Appendix A, page 12', 'for more information, see X', 'click here', 'if you are reading this'. It is not a publication-noun or see/read/click token detector: generic, indefinite or physical uses of the same nouns ('an article about fishing', 'articles of clothing', 'the newspaper article was published yesterday') and the same verbs with a non-document object outside the pointer frame ('see the doctor', 'click the button') stay near zero, while the formulaic pointer frame still fires when its object is a person ('for more information, see the doctor'); the pole's write direction promotes no specific next token (Jacobian kurtosis 3.3) and suppresses the publication vocabulary it has just read ( blog, Blog, Newsletter, Tutorial, ISBN, ISSN, 出版社, 博文).

Fires on the first token that continues a sentence (mostly ',' but also ' (', ' -', ' and', ' however') right after a short, terse main clause that ends on a bare predicate whose complement is left implicit and recoverable from earlier context: VP ellipsis ('It did,', 'Martin doesn't,', 'You can,'), a bare adjective or intransitive verb ('It is possible,', 'They are still looking,', 'it was rarer,'), or a stranded preposition ('a model of,'). It is strongest when the clause is a curt answer to or comment on a topic set up well before (e.g. 'It is possible,' answering a 'Can I...?' question), weak when the clause carries an explicit object or complement ('You can subclass FileInputFormat,'), and near-silent on semicolons, on commas after introductory adverbials ('Yes,', 'In the winter,') and on list commas; leftovers include decimal and thousands separators after a number that could have ended the clause ('$9[.]38', '300[,]000').

The positive pole fires on a third-person personal pronoun or possessive determiner (she/her/he/him/his, more weakly it/its/they/them/their) that refers back to a person or thing already introduced earlier in the passage, and it fires hardest when that referent is not the nearest named person in its clause - a female pronoun after a male name ('Marco praised her work'), or a pronoun sitting after an inanimate noun. It is near zero on first- and second-person pronouns used generically or in instructions ('if you need...', 'I think...'), on expletive 'it', on a pronoun whose referent has not been introduced, and on non-pronoun words.

The positive pole fires on the token that carries a new instance of an already-established parallel series: the second and later members of a coordinate list (England, [[Wales]], Northern Ireland; Google, [[Yahoo]], MSN; flour, [[eggs]], [[sugar]], butter; Paris, [[Berlin]], Rome; He is tall, [[dark]], and handsome) and the varying part of a repeated template (boxHeight/[[boxLength]]/boxWidth, dbUser/[[dbPass]]/dbSchema, pepB-/[[pepN]]-/pepA-, font-oti/[[font-otl]]/font-oto, the repeated digit pair of #434343, the continuation marker \cdots in $k_1,\cdots,k_n$, repeated CSS/table rows), rising from the floor on the first member (0.00 for England, Google, apples, Paris, red) to 0.6-1.5 on interior members. It stays at the floor for those same words outside a series (Wales 0.00, Yahoo 0.00, Windows 0.00, bananas 0.00), for non-enumerative commas (However, ...; In 2019, ...; appositive commas) and for attributive adjective stacks inside a noun phrase (a big, red, shiny hat), and it falls back toward the floor on a short list's final item after a closing 'and'/'or' (bananas 0.08, blue 0.00, timelines 0.00, butter 0.07).

The negative pole fires on the concessive move in evaluative writing: it peaks on a clause-opening concessive marker ('although', 'though', 'even though', 'while', 'despite', 'in spite of', or a concessive opener such as 'sure', 'yes', 'granted', 'it's true') and stays elevated across the clause that marker introduces. The peak is gated by what the writer has just said: it is large only when the preceding sentence makes a strong positive point which the concession then qualifies ('The crew was excellent. Although the boat was old, ...' peaks ~2.4 of the 4.5 max; '...was good...' ~1.7; '...was terrible...' ~0.3; a bare 'Although the room was small, it was clean.' ~0.4), while coordinated contrast ('but', 'however', 'yet', 'nevertheless'), 'because'/'since', 'if', temporal 'while' and praise with no concession following it stay near baseline.

The pole marks the close of a free-standing direct quotation: it peaks on the punctuation token that ends a quotation which occupies its own sentence - typically the comma-glued close ',”', ',"', '!”' or '?”' that hands the utterance back to the narrator, as in '“We need cash,” he said' - and it is near zero on the identical close-quote token when the quotation is embedded in the running sentence (after a reporting verb, 'He said “We need cash,” and left'; as a quoted term, 'The phrase “we need cash,” was used'; or after a mid-sentence colon), on scare quotes closing mid-phrase, on '”' used for inches, on opening quotes, and on a quotation that ends its sentence with '.”' at a paragraph break. Within the free-standing class the strength is graded rather than categorical: it grows with the amount of preceding news-style reporting (about 1.2 with no context, 2.8 after one reportative paragraph, 3.9 after two, up to 5.9 in long articles), is suppressed to near zero when another quotation close falls within a few tokens, and does not depend on what follows the close (the same token fires whether an attribution, a conjunction or another clause comes next).

The negative pole is a weak, graded dial for concrete physical content: it is most active on content words naming physical materials, substances, parts, body parts and small countable things (particles, cells, tissues, rocks, grains, blades, gears, valves, 'texture'; plural people and animals are intermediate) and much less active on large whole artefacts, abstract or social-institutional vocabulary (rules, costs, topics, claims, importance), proper names and function words. It is a dial rather than a crisp detector -- max activation 2.48, 83% of tokens below 0.08, token identity explains only 30% of its variance, and within-concrete vocabulary varies as much as the concrete-abstract gap -- so predict graded activity: physical/technical passages peak around 0.4-1.9, abstract/social prose around 0.1-0.4, and a strongly physical surrounding frame keeps even an abstract slot noun partly active.

Fires on the token that fills a continuation slot opened by the preceding 1-2 tokens: the second subword completing a word stem (Sh->akespeare, Tok->yo, sym->phony), the content word completing a function-word frame (The->noun, I->can, If->x, that->the, submit->your, France->is), or the character/punctuation closing a locally started construct (196->9, range(10->):, np->newline, </->html, report->comma, Lyon->period, name->semicolon). The same token is weak or silent when the preceding token does not open that slot.

This pole fires when the current token is the highly conventional, locally predictable completion of the preceding few tokens — the expected next piece of a common collocation, idiom, code or syntax routine (verb + the, For + i), or stock quantitative/formulaic phrase — and stays low when the same token appears in a weakly constraining or unconventional context.

Fires retrospectively on closing tag prefix tokens (such as "</" or "></") in HTML and XML markup that close an opened tag following element content. Weak background activations on other tokens arise from the SwiGLU double-negative regime, but true positive-regime (g > 0, u > 0) peak activation is specific to closing tag delimiters.

N268− fires on the article or possessive that opens a noun phrase predicating an identification or classification of a referent already in the clause: the appositive after a comma ('Salmonella, the bacteria that cause typhoid fever' 1.91, 'Casablanca, the romantic Moroccan city' 1.87, 'Dymas, a Mariandynian' 0.88), the predicate nominal of a copula, 'as', 'called' or 'one of' ('bx_refinement is the brainchild of…', 'debt repayment as the top priority', 'called a "Standard Type"', 'one of the busiest nights' at ' of' 1.82), and the definite article of an institution or event name ('the National Register of Historic Places' 0.74 vs 0.26 for 'a national register'); it stays at the floor on the same articles and possessives when they open a plain referential noun phrase as subject, object or PP-object of an action clause ('They met a famous actor' 0.0, 'She put a book on the table' 0.0, 'The dog chased the cat' 0.2-0.4). It is retrospective - the peak is on the determiner itself, driven by the comma/copula/name before it (deleting the article 1.91 → 0.33, comma → 'and' 1.67 → 0.68, 'the' → 'these' 1.91 → 0.96) - and its positive pole is a separate offshoot that fires on pre-nominal adjectives and quantifiers introducing new referents ('a new configuration', 'a similar story', 'specific', 'significant', 'some').

The negative pole is a weak, graded marker of the token that opens or separates a further nominal designation: it peaks on the opening parenthesis that gives a short form or alias after a full name ("the World Health Organization (WHO)"), on the ", or X" appositive alias after a name ("...communication disorder, or SCD"), on the comma or final "and"/"or" that separates like-kind nouns in an enumeration ("hammers, chisels and screwdrivers"; the final "or" is strongest), and, less reliably, on the opening quotation mark of a title or term after a naming noun or copula ("the song \"...\"", "their song is \"...\"", "the term \"...\""). The identical punctuation stays near its floor (0.00-0.14) when it does not introduce or separate a nominal designation - quotes after a verb of saying or playing ("they said \"...\"", "they sang \"...\""), parenthetical adverbs, arithmetic parentheses ("f(x)"), clause-joining commas and "and", and adjective lists - but the unit is small in absolute terms (scan maximum 0.85, among the weakest negative-pole maxima in this layer), so read it as a graded bias rather than a reliable detector.

Fires on sentence- or clause-initial anaphoric subjects and contrastive connectives (But/however plus it/they/he/Two/I/we, or those pronouns alone) that open a second proposition which adds another item to, or contrastively qualifies, an entity or claim built up over a longer preceding multi-clause span; the extended prior elaboration and referential continuity are required, not just the local trigger word.

The negative pole is a retrospective detector of numeric field tokens: it fires on the digits of dense numeral runs - patent and application numbers ('No. 2000-159163', '11-325849'), citation volume/issue/page fields ('vol. 338, no. 6109, pp. 963-967'), dates ('Apr 17, 2014', 'October 29, 2018') and hex commit ids ('aa4a605') - and on the space, comma or hyphen that immediately precedes or separates those digits ('No. |2000-159163', 'pp. 963|-967', 'Apr |17'), with activation rising with the local density of digit tokens (mean strength 0.12 with no digit within +-3 tokens versus 0.31 with six). Text without numerals and without clause punctuation stays near zero (mean 0.11); a weaker secondary elevation sits on sentence-final periods and on clause-closing commas, which the same formatting cue explains only in part.

This pole fires on generic continuation tokens (articles, pronouns, conjunctions, prepositions, light adverbs, or routine nouns like 'sample'/'police') when the preceding long-range context describes an institutional procedure that inspects, tests, adjudicates, monitors, or records a person or item — arrest, drug test, trial, audit, detention, medical check, school assessment, or data collection. The same sentence frames describing casual, social, or benign events with no such procedure stay near zero, while the procedure alone (even with a benign verdict) keeps it partly active.

The pole fires retrospectively on the closed-class linker that attaches a noun-phrase argument in expository third-person prose: chiefly the preposition a preceding relational noun or verb selects ('cooperation with', 'studies by', 'injection into', 'paid for by', 'together with', 'compared with'), together with the determiner or coordinator that opens the noun phrase right after it ('by the Rijksmuseum', 'and a group of donors', 'nor the defense'). The noun phrase's own content barely matters (after the same preposition a pronoun, a generic plural and a named institution give the same peak), whereas the same preposition under a head that does not select it ('work for firms', 'studies at the museum') drops sharply, and the identical clause inside informal first-person narrative or a bare one-sentence prompt stays near zero.

L15/N1604+ fires retrospectively on a token that is the conventional, high-expectancy completion of the frame its prefix sets up — a stock collocate, boilerplate slot-filler, parallel repeat, or formulaic opener (degrees->Celsius, password-rule one->number, The->patient/capital/cat, wrote->Hamlet, list->are) — and drops when the same slot takes an unexpected word or the licensing frame is removed, even with the peak token itself unchanged. Only the prefix and the peak token matter, so edits after the peak leave its activation unchanged.

This pole is a technical-documentation register detector rather than a word detector: it is active on tokens inside text written to specify or cite a concrete technical artefact - source code with dotted package paths, template/macro identifiers and nested 'namespace X {' blocks, bibliographic reference entries with author initials, journal abbreviations and volume:page ranges, and definitional statements that introduce a technical term ('A hash table is a data structure that ...', 'The VC-2 video compression standard is ...') - while the same words inside narrative, conversational, journalistic or plain-list prose sit near the floor (measured 0.10-0.25 against 0.5-1.45 for the technical cases). Within a firing passage the peak lands on whichever token carries the most specific content, so the same token ranges over the whole scale: ' is' scores 0.78 after '(MRF)' but 0.02 in 'for it is one of the many ways', and ' standard' scores 0.91 in 'The VC-2 video compression standard is an open free-use standard' but 0.00 in every other occurrence in the scan corpus.

N4170− fires when the text refers to the older, incumbent or pre-digital form of a practice, technology or institution: either the modifier that labels it ('traditional', 'classic', 'classical', 'conventional', 'old', 'old-fashioned', 'analog', 'manual', 'film', 'previously', 'historically', 'used to') or the predicate that spells out how that older arrangement worked ('relies on', 'still based on', 'was delivered through'), as in 'replace the traditional cuff-based monitors', 'Updates used to be delivered through a separate software update app' or 'the disappearance of a linear path', whereas 'usual', 'customary', 'standard', 'modern', 'new', 'advanced' and 'newer' in the identical slots add nothing. It is retrospective and context-gated: the peak is on the modifier itself or on the preposition/copula of its phrase, and the same words stay low (0.1-1.2) unless the modern counterpart or the superseded category is already established in the preceding text (2.1-5.5 when it is: 'Advertising is cheap and precise. Traditional advertising is expensive' 2.98 vs the reversed order 0.70), while its output direction promotes exactly the old-world vocabulary ('paper', 'books', 'chalk', 'film', 'handwritten', 'analog', 'telephone', 'clergy', 'railroad') and suppresses modern-digital words ('internet', 'online', 'digital', 'smartphone', 'IoT', 'WiFi', 'Instagram', 'social media').

N4506+ fires when a specific referent has just been classified as a KIND - a nationality, ethnicity, religion, era, style, school, material or type ('German', 'Jewish', 'Catholic', 'Victorian', 'Gothic', 'Carolingian', 'socialist', 'rural', 'diesel', 'traditionalist') - and the clause then names the domain, respect or span in which that kind holds, with the peak on the preposition or possessive that links them and staying high over the scope phrase that follows ('English in his habits' 3.6, 'Italian in his tastes' 5.0, 'Swiss in its ownership' 4.3, 'Catholic in her sympathies' 4.1, 'French in character' 3.1, 'Gothic in its proportions' 2.8, 'Victorian in its proportions' 2.4, 'rural in its customs' 2.0). Both halves are needed: bare kind predication with no scope ('He was German.' 0.30, 'The building was Gothic.' 0.22, 'The wine was French.' 0.16), the identical scope frame filled with a scalar adjective ('illegible in its script' 0.22, 'cautious in its rhetoric' 0.15, 'happy in his drinking' 0.02), group-level generalizations ('Victorians are known for their morality' 0.06) and eventive reports of a referent's property ('their products reached forty markets' 0.16, 'its holdings were itemized' 0.03, 'its merchandise filled three storefronts' 0.02) all stay far below the 0.58 active threshold, and the response is retrospective - the peak sits on the linking token itself, rises over the scope phrase that has already been read, and zero-ablating the pole leaves next-token predictions essentially unchanged (next-token KL ~2e-4 in the scan's measurement).

The negative pole fires retrospectively when a digit- or CJK-numeral quantity stating how many duplicate or batch items were printed, built, released, shipped, sold, grossed, or quantified with just/fewer-than/per/many completes, peaking on the final digit, the batch noun (copies, 册, theaters, convertibles, pair, units) or the closing particle; it stays weak or silent for spelled-out English cardinals (three hundred, a dozen, four), unit prices in words, measurement magnitudes, dates/identifiers, generic furniture-order tallies with comprised/delivery framing, and count-free text, whose short-corpus bumps (salt/day/./he, all <=0.5, <4% of the 14.06 scan max) are background noise.

This sparse detector pole fires on written and online reference material: instructions and the digital objects they act on (click, open, download, save, follow a file, page, link, button, chart or schedule), step lists, glossary or definition passages, and a page's own furniture (last-updated, published and access dates, view counts, copyright lines, tables of contents and '||' / '»' navigation separators). It stays at baseline on narrative fiction, news and argumentative prose, on physical-task instructions such as cooking, carpentry or gardening, and on ordinary sentences about people or physical objects.

The pole fires on the token that completes a multi-word unit, not on the token's identity: the last element of a compound name or pre-modified bare NP ('British scientists' 1.63 vs 'The scientists' 0.00; 'Golden State Warriors' 1.69 then 2.64), the second token of a fixed multiword preposition ('according to' 1.77, 'compared with' 0.39 vs 'compared to' 0.21), a separator that closes a dateline/header ('MANILA (Reuters) -' 3.26 vs the same slot filled by a comma 0.62), a complementizer or connective that closes the matrix clause ('ruled that' 0.30, 'five, then' 0.44, 'half, and' 0.59), and the period or newline that ends a sentence or paragraph (peak 0.5-1.8 in about 40% of the corpus's declarative sentences, 0.00-0.14 in the rest). It stays near zero on the same surface tokens when they open rather than close a unit (a comma in the dateline slot, 'ruled:' 0.13, the first element 'British' 0.03, interior content words after the unit closes), and the whole completed span must be present: ablating any single content word inside it drops the peak by 60-90%.

Fires on a token whose text begins with the letter sequence 'str' (any case, with or without a leading space or hyphen), strongest (about 0.5-1.0 of max) when that token is a bare sub-word fragment such as 'str', ' Str', 'Str', '-str', ' strat', ' stre' that opens a longer word or name (stratospheric, Stringer, Stroud, Lindström, strait, single-stranded, stratification); whole-word 'str' tokens are weaker (' string', ' strategic', ' strict', ' stretch' about 0.1-0.6, depending on context), very common whole words (' strong', ' street', ' structure') are near zero, and tokens without the 'str' onset (' St', 'thr', ' D') are inactive. It is retrospective: the activation reads the current token's spelling, with little dependence on earlier context, and the Jacobian lens (kurtosis 3.2) promotes no coherent next-token set.

Retrospectively peaks on the second token of a frequent two-token chunk (usually a content word plus a function word, determiner plus noun, or subword continuation), driven mainly by the immediately preceding token; the same peak token after an incongruent predecessor is inactive.

The negative pole fires when a comparative is used in a definite or clause-initial frame in a short clause: 'the more/less + ADJECTIVE' (peaks on 'more'/'less' and on the adjective after it, e.g. 'The more expensive model is better.', 'The more detailed analysis revealed the problem.'), the 'the X-er, the Y-er' correlative ('The more you practice, the better you get.', 'The bigger the better.'), the sentence-initial attributive 'the ADJ-er + noun' (strongest for bigger/stronger/larger/higher/faster/lighter/longer/louder/better; cheaper/lower/older/taller/sooner are near-threshold), and the appositive 'NP, on the other hand, VP' pivot (peak on 'other'); a short adverbial lead-in ('In practice, the more detailed analysis...') preserves firing, a subject-verb lead-in does not. It is inactive (below 0.25 x max) for predicative 'X is ADJ-er than Y' with an explicit than-target, quantity 'more/less + plural noun', superlatives (most/best/least), bare intensifiers (very/extremely), isolated non-English comparative markers (更/más/plus), contracted 'what's more', mid-clause 'the more ADJ' after a subject-verb, and sentence-initial adverbial 'On the other hand, ...'; the two strongest unmatched scan peaks ('but' 5.47 after 'Like flares', ')' 4.18 after a statistical parenthetical) need their full multi-sentence contexts and are acknowledged leftovers.

The pole fires while a passage is accumulating distinct national-scale referents - names of countries, of capitals or world cities that belong to different countries, national currencies, nationality adjectives, or international organisations - and it peaks on the comma, 'and', 'to' or other function word at the boundary where the next such referent is added (or on the first subword of that name), so the peak lands on the linker rather than on the name itself; strength rises with the number of distinct nations already on its left: one referent or a bare two-place relation stays at 0.1-0.75, two reach 1.1-1.9, three or four 1.7-3.7, and dense report, ranking or table lists 4.4-5.2. It stays at its floor when the enumeration remains inside a single nation (UK cities 0.74, US states 0.28, Canadian provinces and English counties 0.2-0.7, German Laender 0.14), when the listed items are not national-scale (animals 0.02, ordinary objects 0.07, car models 0.58, grape varieties 1.02, rivers 1.05), and on a single place name ('France is a country' 0.52) or a bare two-place relation ('between Germany and Brazil' 0.75); a list of personal names in the same enumerative frame sits in between (0.97-2.7) and never reaches the 3-5 band that country, world-city and international-organisation lists reach.

The N1073- pole is a document-reference-apparatus detector: it fires on a token when the surrounding span is a fixed-format reference or metadata field rather than prose - above all a bibliographic citation or page/volume reference ('The American Naturalist, 152(4), 495-506', 'pp. 495-506', 'Vol 129, 277-288', 'Page No. 162', 'p. 26', '108 Stat. 125', '41(6):1180-1186'), but also word/page counts ('(The entire section is 448 words.)', 'Words: 928. Pages: 4.'), datelines and forum bylines ('Tuesday, May 21, 2013'), image credits ('Jupiterimages/BananaStock/Getty Images', 'Creatas/Creata'), site names ('newscientist.com') and site widgets ('1 Answer | Add Yours'), with strength graded by how canonically the string matches such a template (an invented journal name, or Roman-numeral or spelled-out field values, keeps it under 1). Token identity supplies only a weak floor of about 0.2-0.5 of the pole's 4.04 scale (' almost', ' nearly', ' Golden' fire weakly anywhere); the reference frame is what lifts a peak to 1.5-4.0, and the same numbers, names and punctuation in running prose, generic page chrome ('Cookie Policy', 'Share on Facebook'), labelled product specs ('Weight: 860 g', 'Goals: 12. Assists: 3.'), addresses, code or empty templates do not fire it.

Fires on the non-final digits of a large numeral written with a thousands separator in running prose (prices, populations, square footage, viewer counts), peaking on the 1st and 2nd digit after the ',' (any digit value, not just '0'; weaker with '.'), and staying near zero on the last digit of a group, on spelled-out numbers ('seven thousand', '$25 million'), and on years and other short numbers. Weaker secondary triggers are the pandoc citation opener '[@' (but not '[#', '[$' or '(@'), 'World/world' in set phrases ('Book of World Records', "the world's first"), and the article ' a' right after a preposition that opens a modified noun phrase ('by a combined', 'in a statistical tie'; ' the' there gives about half as much); preceding news-style prose roughly doubles the response compared with chit-chat or code context.

In prose that reports experimental or debugging results, fires on the last token of a clause's subject (head noun, closing ',' or ')' of an appositive or relative clause, or a pre-verbal 'also'/'it'), when that subject names a manipulation, agent or tested condition (gene knock-out, drug treatment, inhibitor, oligomers, 'when I comment it out') and the predicate about to follow will report its observed effect. It is strongest when a negative or contrastive outcome is set up ('None of the ...', 'however', '... did not'), and weak or absent when the same noun is an object or a procedural or descriptive mention ('we stored the oligomers', 'read-out of the gene') or appears in non-experimental narrative.

Peaks on the verb, preposition, or determiner that completes a measurable-quantity frame (a measurable subject such as unemployment, revenue, electrons, or galaxy plus a change, carry, or quantity construction), preparing a precise numeral or measure phrase such as a percent, billion, times, half, or charge amount within the next few tokens. The same trigger word with a non-measurable subject, or a vague-quantity continuation instead of a precise one, stays weak.

Fires retrospectively when the current token completes a locally highly predictable chunk, i.e. the token is strongly constrained by the immediately preceding 1-3 tokens (fixed idiom, collocation, number-plus-unit, code alias reuse, or formulaic phrase).

L17/N3698+ fires on the tokens that carry the non-linguistic payload of machine-formatted text: digits inside multi-digit numeric literals (the '0' of port 5000, of 62.5%, of -Xmx1024m), the '%' of a printf-style format verb, and the internal fragments or punctuation of identifiers, URLs and config strings (the 'Base' of DefaultBaseURI, '=-' in jvmargs=-Xmx1024m, '[it' in properties[it], 'Name' of sServerName). The same digits, percents and fragments embedded in ordinary narrative prose ('the port was 5000' after a descriptive sentence, '100 % of the students', 'ten point five percent') leave it at or below 0.5 of its 3.98 max, so the pole reads the code/quantitative register built up over the preceding tens of tokens rather than the token identity alone.

L17/N4098+ fires where a text says or implements that ONE item is being taken out of a source: in prose the extraction verb itself (took, extracted, withdrew, snatched, plucked, seized, grabbed, removed, fetched, retrieved, pulled, picked, brought, got, Portuguese 'pega' - 'He walked to the shelf and took the red folder down' peaks at 6.4 on ' took' while the identical frame with left/touched/inspected/pushed stays at 0.76), and in code the call or operator that hands a single value across ('$this->_stmt->fetch(...)' 3.9, 'scanner.nextLine()' 3.7, 'getPropriedadeLimpar' 3.3 on the '::', '$_SESSION' 2.2 on ' $_', 'CACHE.get(id)' 1.9, '__getitem__', 'pop', 'RemoveFlag', 'load_command_class', 'Retrieves ...', and the ' =' of the item-at-a-time read loop 'while ($data = $this->_stmt->fetch(...))' 3.9). It is near zero when the same text acts on the whole collection instead of one item ('fetchAll'/foreach, array_map, .mapNotNull, .Items/.Rows/.Clear, list.entries: 0.01-0.35 - the regime where this neuron's negative pole fires at 1.7-8.3), and near zero on idiomatic or non-extraction uses of the same verbs ('It took two hours' 0.20, 'took the bus' 0.26, 'took a photo' 0.23, pushed/left/found/dropped 0.76); the unexplained leftovers are the weak (1.2-1.8) article/preposition tokens of Spanish and Portuguese code explanations (' la', ' el', ' de', ' uma').

This pole fires on the content word that felicitously completes an open complement slot — the object or complement licensed by a preceding verb, preposition, or fixed phrase (opened→door, of→France, far→away) — and stays near zero when the same word appears as a subject/topic or when the slot holds a semantically infelicitous filler.

This pole marks the backbone of a clause's main assertion: it peaks on the subject/topic head (The stock/cat/river, protons, one pill), on the head of the main predicate (lexical verbs like sat/fell/sits/print, copulas is/are, and measure or frequency complements like three, 12 percent, 100 degrees, all), and on tokens that launch the next clause or enumerated item (which, and/while, first-conjunct commas, sentence-final periods). It stays near zero on determiners, on backgrounded definite objects, and on highly predictable continuations (times after three, open after is, flooded after river), so the same noun fires strongly as subject but weakly as object.

Fires retrospectively on the current token when it delivers the distinctive specifying payload of a factual or instructional statement -- the property predicated of a subject (boils), the unit completing a number (billion, times), the day completing opening hours (Tuesday), or the connective completing an event (until) -- strongest when the token completes a subject-predicate or number-unit pairing, and only weakly on the same surface token in episodic or non-factual use. Its output suppresses equivalence markers (same-family) and weakly promotes closure markers (finally / 最后), consistent with marking newly specified content rather than predicting a particular next token.

The negative pole fires on the token that completes the stem of a Latin/Romance word the text is still writing, i.e. the piece on which the word in progress stops being stem material and only an ending can follow ('iter-' in iteración, ' administr-' in administrating, 'eler-' in decelerations, 'ug-' in centrifugation, ' demand-' in French demandent, 'cancel-' in Portuguese cancelou, 'ibr-' in calibrating); it is silent on earlier pieces of the same word while the stem is still incomplete (' centrif' before '-ug-', 'dec' before '-eler-', ' contr' before '-ari-'), on the same strings when they end a complete word ('demand' in 'The union will demand safer conditions', 'inform' in 'Please inform the committee', 'reconsider' in 'We should reconsider the plan'), on whole words that arrive in one token ('iteration', 'administration', 'centrifuge') and on non-Latinate fragments ('fenugreek'). It is retrospective, not lookahead: the peak is fixed by the prefix alone (the same ' demand' piece reads 10.79 after a French prefix and 0.03 after an English one, and deleting the ending after 'reconsider' leaves its 6.33 unchanged), and zero-ablating the pole spreads a small loss over the whole ending family (aggregate KL 2.1e-03, shifted tokens 'at', 'ation', 'ating', 'ar', 'ados', 'atively', concentration below the 0.5 gate) instead of concentrating it on one upcoming token.

Fires on the word that opens an argument slot (a preposition such as to/on/for/of/at, the conjunction 'or', or a transitive operation verb such as maps/lists/click/attach) in technical, computing or scientific text when that slot is about to be filled by an inanimate technical entity (a file, directory, UI element, key, cable, query, feature or stimulus), e.g. 'No such file [or] directory', 'right click [on]', 'skipping queries [for]', 'Visual attention [to] features', 'The config file [maps]'. It stays near zero when the same frame expects a person as filler (explain/hand/introduce X to, talked to, popular with, 'No such person or') or on content nouns themselves; consistent with this, its output suppresses person nouns (' people', ' users', ' developers', ' students').

The pole fires on the indefinite determiner 'some' (and much more weakly on 'any') where it is used as a hedge that leaves the amount, degree or kind of something unspecified - the reading of 'need some help', 'for some time', 'some form of debt', 'some kind of', 'is there some way', 'showed some interest' - and its write at that position is the matching vague-classifier set ('kind', 'sort', 'type', 'form', 'way', 'time') instead of the specific noun the model would otherwise name. It stays at floor on the very same token where 'some' merely picks out particular countable individuals that are met, bought, seen or counted ('I met some friends', 'I bought some books', 'in some cases', 'for some reason'), on a sentence-initial 'Some' with nothing before it, on every other quantifier (several, many, few, a few, certain), and on compounds (someone, something, somewhat, somehow); and because the peak is on the determiner itself only the text before it can matter, so changing the word after 'some' never changes the value.

Retrospective detector for a token that is the conventional, highly predictable continuation of the immediately preceding context: the formulaic verb after a politeness marker (Please/Kindly -> remember), the default column name after SELECT, the fixed preposition after a measure noun (cups -> of), the alias slot after 'as' in an import, a subword finishing a word, or a sentence-final period closing a completed clause, peaking on that continuation token itself with fully local input attribution. The identical surface token outside its frame stays weak or silent (remember 1.68 -> 0.10 after They; name 0.49 -> 0.02 after My; of 0.33 -> 0.00 after dogs), which a fires-on-trigger-tokens baseline cannot predict; although the output direction strongly promotes ':' (Jacobian z +16.9), no peak in this scan is followed by ':', so no lookahead is claimed.

This pole fires retrospectively on the first chunk of a fixed multi-token expression, a lexicalized compound (sun|spots, space|walks, leather|backs, pain|killers), a fixed title or name (Moon|Patrol), or a set collocation (buzz|word, Down|fall), when preceding context primes that exact expression: repeated prior mentions boost it strongly and a constraining frame suffices with no repetition. It is near-silent on the completion chunk itself and on the same word used outside any fixed expression, so its peak always lands just before the predictable continuation rather than on it.

This pole fires retrospectively when the current token completes a conventional, stereotyped multi-token construction: a fixed idiom or collocation (because of, not guilty, golden brown), boilerplate or code idiom (Hello-world closing tag, range(, def-header return, fairy-tale adjunct comma), a canonical memorized proposition (boiling-point Celsius, Where-are-you-going), or punctuation closing a complete clause. Strength scales with stereotypicality (canonical chunks ~0.6-0.8, frame-preserving substitutions ~0.2-0.3), and the same tokens in novel compositional uses (weather-report Celsius measured 0.000, felt guilty 0.000, return the book 0.004, brown fox 0.07, abbreviation dots ~0.05) stay near silent, so the claim beats the token-identity confound (R2 69%). The Jacobian lens promotes 'cost' tokens (kurtosis 3.7, near-Gaussian) that never follow the peaks, so the effect is retrospective detection, not lookahead.

Fires retrospectively on the digits of a year (its first one or two digits, e.g. the '1' and '0' of 1087), or of a century ordinal ('12th'), when the numeral dates a past event or entity in a historical, ecclesiastical or encyclopedic sentence: a temporal phrase attached to a historical subject ('the abbey was built/founded in 1087' 23.4, 'the king died in 1087 at Rouen' 19.4, 'from 1087 to 1100' 22.9, 'the abbey grew in the 12th century' 17.3 of a 23.1 scale), where older years fire higher than modern ones (1087 ~23, 2019 ~14) and a modern or commercial subject fires much less (the company was founded in 1087 ~12, the website was built in 1087 ~0.3). It stays near zero (0.2-2) on the same numerals as quantities, counts, page or room numbers or bare subjects ('the abbey housed 1087 monks', 'the price was 1087 dollars', '1087 was a good year for the abbey'), when the year is fronted to the sentence start with no historical context before it ('In 1087 the abbey was finished' alone 2.2, but 19.3 after 'The monks were devout.'), and on brackets in code, except a secondary mode on the bracket opening a shell test after a conditional keyword ('if [', 'while [', ' [[' fires 12-18 while 'if (' and ordinary brackets stay near zero).

The negative pole fires where the model is mid-way through a formulaic multi-token frame rather than composing a new phrase: the determiner, possessive or particle that follows keep/kept/keeping/stay or have/had in a fixed collocation or possessive-object frame ('keep a close eye', 'keep an eye', 'Keep in touch', 'keep up to date', 'keep in mind', 'kept them waiting', 'keep his hands free', 'had his camera', 'have your home'), and by the same logic the second element of a fixed technical string ('-get' in apt-get, the ' -p'/' --restart' flags of a command line, 'e-book', 'Privacy Policy', 'Magn Reson Med') or a key-value separator (':' '=') inside a machine-readable listing. It is near zero when the same words occur in novel combinations ('kept the receipt', 'hold his hands', 'watch the report closely', 'maintain a close eye', the hyphens of 'well-known' or '3-2'), so the formulaic frame rather than the word or the punctuation is the trigger; the sentence-initial 'Keep' form reaches its peak only when the document has already set up a promotional/newsletter register, consistent with most of the input attribution lying far to the left.

L19/N1638- fires wherever the text names the source being cited in a report - a person or their role, an organisation's mouthpiece, or a document/study/report - at the point that phrase is the subject of the clause: it builds across the phrase as the phrase is specified ('a spokesman' 4.0 -> 'a spokesman for the group' 9.5, 13.5 in the scan's top snippet) and peaks on the phrase's last token, immediately before the reporting verb ('..., a source' 8.1, '..., he' 8.0, 'police officials' 6.1, 'the project's team leader' 6.9, 'a CIBC study from earlier this year' 6.4, 'the report' 7.6), most strongly in the postposed attribution tag after quoted or reported speech. It is near zero on the same words in any other role - as an object ('We fired a spokesman for the group' 0.5, 'We questioned a CIBC study from earlier this year' 0.1, 'We called Smith about the deal' 0.1), as a bare name or title subject of an ordinary sentence ('Smith said the deal was done' 0.4 over the whole prompt, 'The senator said the deal was done' 0.4, 'After the meeting, Smith said the deal was done' 0.4, all below the 3.4 active threshold) - and on the reporting verb itself (' said' is 0.0 at every peak); its output direction does promote exactly that verb family (' said'/' says'/' told', Jacobian z 12.2, kurtosis 5.5) and it lifts P(' said') when intact (0.288 vs 0.231 ablated on 'a spokesman for the group'), but the protocol's lookahead probe returns retrospective (concentration 0.40 < 0.5, KL ~1e-3) because the write is spread across the family, so this is recorded as a retrospective detector of the attribution-source noun phrase rather than a lookahead for a single token.

Fires retrospectively when the current token sits inside a paratextual reference or document-metadata span: a citation locator (author-year with p./pp. plus page number, volume(issue):pages, chapter:verse range, statute number, et al. plus year) or a navigational/extent footer (See-all-reviews, Click-here-for cross-reference, section word/page counts), built up over long preceding context. Plain numbers in ordinary prose without the reference frame do not drive it.

This retrospective unit detects surface landing or contact events and inland terrestrial features (e.g., river, lake, tree, landed on), contrasting with its negative pole which strongly fires on downward motion, descent, and bottom or sea-level positions (e.g., fell, dropped, down, sea level). Through its output projection, positive activations suppress upcoming tokens denoting downward direction or descent (down, lower, below, and Chinese 下 compounds).

This pole fires on the very first token of the input when that token is a structural function word or code keyword that opens an incomplete multi-token structure (articles, demonstratives, prepositions, subordinators, conjunctions, interrogatives, auxiliaries, or statement keywords such as import/from/def); it stays silent when the input opens with a content word (proper/common nouns, lexical verbs, interjections, discourse adverbs) and when the same structural tokens appear anywhere past absolute position 0.

Qwen2.5-0.5B L19/N611+ prepares a closing delimiter: it fires on the last token(s) of a typographic insertion embedded in running text - an enumerated list label ('(b)', '2)'), a parenthesised code such as a phone area code ('(212)'), or the interior of emphasis/quote/markup ('_very_', '*will override*', '[getting a divorce]', "'password'") - where that insertion's closer (')', ']', '_', '**', '"') is the token the model will emit next, and it stays near-silent in ordinary prose and in grammatical parentheticals such as '(which met on Tuesday)' even when a ')' is likely. Zeroing the pole at those positions removes probability from exactly that closer (']' after '[getting', '_' after '_very', '**' after '**very'), matching the Jacobian lens's promoted ')'/']'/'”'; a weaker, diffuse component over legal/licence boilerplate has no delimiter nearby and is left unexplained.

The pole fires on the token that carries a character-level piece of a machine-formatted literal rather than a word: the digits of an IP/port/host address written in a machine slot ('port=5432', 'Port 5432', 'listens on 5432', 127.0.0.1), URL scheme and path components ('://', '/LICENSE' in http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0), and byte-fallback tokens that decode to '�' (partial UTF-8 bytes of a CJK character the tokenizer splits - its scan maximum, 6.31, is a partial byte of 风/向 inside a Java comment). It stays at the ~0.1 floor for whole words, ordinary prose, whole non-ASCII characters (温度), bare domains and email addresses, and the same digits in non-address frames ('the order number is 5432', 'the config sets timeout=5432'); its negative pole is the opposite register, peaking on ordinary function words in narrative prose (' out' 10.1, ' for' 9.8, ' a' 8.0, ' under', ' in').

The pole fires retrospectively on the token that completes a memorized two-token chunk from a narrow inventory: blow/blew/back-forms + up; bump/crash/rush/walk/run + into; white/black/brown/blind + man; Big + Bang/House; title-case Back + To; Banach + space; background + -color/-position; Blues + cript; and continuations of split b-initial stems (bak|grunn, bas|emen, Ban|ach, Bak|ayaro, back|garden/pedal). The identical completion after a different head stays silent (grew/fixed/broke + up; burst/step/look/drive + into; tall/big/dark/deaf/young + man; White + House; foreground + -color; Hilbert/parking + space), as do b-initial heads outside the inventory (brave knight, Brooklyn Bridge, batter/Bundt, bootstrap); the licensing head can sit several tokens back (back it/them up; backed up the truck into).

N3833- is a sparse, retrospective two-token-chunk detector: it peaks on the second token of a pair this model stores as one lexical unit, either the continuing piece of a word Qwen's tokenizer split (' Concor'+'de', ' disc'+'ursive', ' dispos'+'als', ' dis'+'joint'+'ed', ' part'+'ing') or the second word of a frozen collocation ('do'+'so', 'do'+'best', 'dispose'+'of', 'differ'+'from', 'similar'+'to', 'daughter'+'of', 'political'+'will', 'Hudson'+'Bay'). It reads the pair and not the token - the same second token after an unmemorized partner sits at the floor (' so' after do/does/doing 1.0-2.0 vs after say/think/hope/believe 0.0-0.1; ' of' after dispose 1.8 vs after consist/think/talk/approve 0.06-0.18; 'ed' after disjoint 1.95 vs after joint 0.0) and membership is idiosyncratic rather than frequency- or semantics-based ('similar to'/'identical to' fire while 'equal to'/'close to' do not; 'dispose of' fires while 'consist of' does not; 'New York', 'make sure', 'in spite of' and 'part of' are inactive), so label active only the listed pairs, their exact repeats, and further completions of the same split words, and label the opening fragment of a split word (' Con', ' disc', ' dispos', ' disjoint') inactive.

Retrospective detector for the orthographic chunk mal (any case) isolated at a token-piece boundary: strongly active (about 9-19 of max 18.5) on bare word-initial pieces ' mal'/'Mal'/'mal' and standalone all-caps ' MAL' (malnutrition, maligned, Maldives, Malfoy), moderately active (about 5-7) on the word-internal piece 'imal' in antimalarial and on the whole-word Latinate adjectives ' dental' (~5) and ' medical' (~6.5, weaker ~1-2.5 on ' linear'/' medicinal'), and secondarily moderately (about 5-11) on split-off ' bene'/' ben'/' Beng', the name ' Ben', and ' mathematical'. It stays below ~4 (usually <1, so a trigger-free corpus peaks below 1) when the letters are fused inside one token (' malaria', ' malware', ' malfunction', ' mall', ' Malta'/'Mali'/'Malcolm', ' benefit'/'beneficial'/'benign'/'bench'/'Benjamin', ' benef' in benefactor ~2), on ' Ben' in 'Big Ben'/'Uncle Ben' or as the very first token, and on ordinary words.

The positive pole is a lookahead for the noun that sums up a person's or organisation's performance - 'record', 'track record', 'reputation', 'history' - and it spikes on the word immediately before that noun: on 'track' in 'a track record', on '2' in 'a 7-2 record', on 'poor' in 'a poor record on safety', on the possessive in "a firm's reputation", on 'long' in 'the orchestra's long association' (81% of its scan spikes fall below half on the very next token, median ratio 0.09). Its output pushes ' record'/' track' - the whole Jacobian-lens top ten is record/track variants, and zero-ablating the pole removes 0.22-0.26 of P(' record') where that word is due - while it stays silent when 'record' means a document or a mark ('a world record' 0.03 vs 'a criminal record' 7.3), when the same modifier is predicative ('the record on safety is poor' 1.5 vs 'a poor record' 15.6), and when the head noun is concrete or forward-looking ('a detailed plan', 'a clear vision', 'a new product': 0.0). Note the protocol's averaged measure_lookahead gate returns False (KL 0.020) because the pole is silent at most positions; the lookahead is concentrated at the roughly 1-in-300 tokens where a record noun is due.

The pole is a retrospective detector for tokens that complete or establish a relational/structural link between two semantic units. It fires on prepositions (on, to, from), conjunctions (and), and terminating punctuation (., ,) when they connect a preceding element to a following one - e.g., 'sat [[on]] the mat', 'SELECT name [[FROM]] users', 'A and [[B]]', 'sentence [[.]]'. The input attribution (50% on peak token) and token identity confound (R²=0.63) are consistent with this: the neuron responds to the token's identity in a connecting structural position, not to any particular semantic content of the linked elements. The Jacobian lens promoting action verbs (draw, soak, kill) reflects what the pole writes to the residual stream downstream, not what it detects.

This pole fires retrospectively when the current token delivers the resolving payload of a frame set up by the preceding tokens: the statement executing a just-opened code header, the predicate verb or head noun completing its subject/modifier frame, or sentence-final punctuation closing a complete proposition. It stays low on the frame-setting words themselves, and the same surface token goes quiet when its frame is removed or the unit is left unclosed.
