The negative pole fires on a form of the verb 'be' (was, were, is, are, been, be, being; French est/ete) whose subject denotes an animate being: strongly for a person - a name, he/she/they, or a human noun ('the officer was' 11.0, 'the soldier was' 10.5, 'the suspect was' 9.8, 'the workers were' 9.2, 'the children were' 6.0) and more weakly for an animal ('the dog was' 5.4, 'the cat was' 5.3) - while an inanimate object, institution or abstraction as subject leaves it at baseline or in a weak middle band ('the report was' 0.0, 'the theory was' 0.0, 'the weather was' 0.0, 'it was' 0.0, 'there was' 0.0, 'the building was' 2.7, 'the company was' 5.2), and a non-'be' predicate about a person also leaves it at baseline ('the man went' 0.7, 'he said' 0.0, 'he had' 0.0, 'the suspect fled' 0.0). The same animacy response fires more weakly on animate nouns themselves, but only where the surrounding text already makes those people the topic of a statement - quantified or categorised groups ('229 patients' 10.4, '193 women', Wikipedia 'Category:People' / 'Category:Writers' lines 7-11) and objects of verbs like 'interviewed' ('the people' 8.8) - and not on inanimate nouns in the same frames ('229 samples' 2.7, 'Category:Films' 0.0, 'the samples' 0.8); its write direction promotes the forward-looking past participles (killed, arrested, injured, convicted, elected, appointed, diagnosed), and its opposite (positive) pole is weaker (scan max 8.8) and shares the be-form preference.

The pole fires when the current token is the canonical completion of a multi-token unit primed by the preceding 2-6 tokens: a subword finishing a primed proper name (Se+ine, Tok+yo), a digit continuing a fact-primed number stem (0 after 'Water boils at 1'), or a word completing a fixed collocation or schema (not guilty, mg of, a negative, a kingdom, the river). The same token in a neutral context, or a schema-violating substitute in the primed context, stays quiet.

This pole fires, in graded fashion, on the token that completes a locally familiar chunk: a fixed idiom or collocation ('three times a day', 'at sea level', 'are often called', 'the central bank'), a morphological or digit continuation ('re-election', '12', '3.9'), a code frame ('return' after a def header and indent), or punctuation closing a formulaic opening ('In 1969,', 'far away,', 'Paris, which'). The same surface token in a novel or weakly cued context activates weakly or not at all, so contextual predictability from the preceding 1-3 tokens, not token identity alone, drives it; sentence-initial common nouns after 'The' fit only weakly and sit at the low end of its range.

L21/N1368+ is a non-English-text feature: it runs hot through Dutch prose (mean about 1.0 over the whole Dutch scan document, and most tokens of a Dutch paragraph land at 0.5-5, peaking at 4.5-8.7 on Dutch words and word pieces - 'het' 3.2, 'jaar' 7.0, 'en' 4.6, 'ige' 4.5, 'ig' in 'nodig' 8.7, 'in' 8.6, 'moet' 4.7), while the same content in English (max 0.14), German (0.78), French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Danish, Swedish or Norwegian stays at the noise floor; Afrikaans, Low German, Limburgish and Indonesian/Malay behave like Dutch, so the trigger is the language of the context and not its topic. Inside English and code it instead peaks (2-7) on a small family of rare word-initial pieces of names and identifiers ('Dun' in Dunster 7.9, 'Min' in Minster 6.3, 'MN' in MNIST 7.2, 'Mult'/'mult' in multivariate 5.2, 'Mc' in McNeill 3.8, '.db' in django.db 5.6, 'vec' in vecS 5.3, '="@' 4.1, 'fetch' 4.0), with 'Dover', 'London', 'Cheltenham', 'Zbigniew', 'multiple' and ordinary English prose staying below 0.4-0.9; its negative pole marks explicit date and numeric range spans ('from 1966 to 2015' -21.7, 'September 3 through 6' -27.7), and the pole's output direction suppresses 'through'/'via' in every language (logit-lens z -15.4 for ' through').

The pole detects reader-facing service copy: it fires where a website, app, shop or company states what it does, offers or enables for its users, peaking on the connective or light function word that opens the purpose, capability or benefit clause (usually ' to', ' can', ' and', ' you', ' by', ' we'), sometimes on a word of the promise itself ('Keep', 'customers', 'better'). It is strongest (8-12) on cookie-consent and privacy-notice sentences ('We use cookies to ...', 'Our partners use cookies to ensure ...', 'This website uses cookies and similar technologies to ...'), moderate (3-6) on app, feature and benefit copy ('the app uses your camera/location to ...', 'other users can recognize you ...', 'our parties are a great way to make new friends', 'we'll keep you notified'), and weak (<2) on the very same tokens in detached narration, news and scientific reporting with a purpose infinitive ('the factory uses coal to ...', 'the committee met on Tuesday to discuss ...', 'she used a knife to ...'), so token identity alone does not explain it: 97% of the scan's 2,791 ' to' occurrences stay below 3. A weaker (<5) leftover fires on rare Greek-root technical subwords (pharmacophores, Sephadex, electroencephalography) and a few non-English function pieces.

L21/N3648+ fires on a large expanse of sea or air named or measured as a space: ocean and sea names ('Atlantic', 'Pacific', 'Indian', 'Ocean', 'Sea'), marine features ('waters', 'continental shelf', 'coastline'), and the distances, areas, coordinates and altitudes that span them ('miles', 'nautical miles', 'km', 'square kilometres', 'degrees north'). Peaks are highest when such a space is bounded or claimed ('territorial sea', 'territorial waters', 'exclusive economic zone', 'extends 200 km', 'airspace extends 200 km'), weaker for land or generic extents measured the same way, and near zero when the same words name objects, food or abstractions ('the kitchen shelf', 'Indian food', 'Atlantic blue', '159 members', 'the economic zone'); the pole reacts to the expanse it has just read, not to an upcoming token.

The negative pole is the active regime of a bilingual 'appraisal' concept neuron: it fires when the running text names an evaluation of something — a rating, judgment, verdict, review/reviewer, evaluation, appraisal, award or acclaim (Chinese 评价/评分/评级) — peaking on that word or on the function word one or two tokens after it (e.g. 'The [[rating]] was', 'a rating [[of]] four and a half stars', 'Two [[reviewers]] independently'), and stays near zero for process/reporting vocabulary (audit, inspection, measurement, analysis, report) and for neutral description even in identical frames. It is retrospective, not lookahead: its output direction demotes exactly the vocabulary it detects (rating/evaluation/criteria rank 4/8/15 in w_out·W_U and are suppressed with z≈-12, while its 'promoted' list is the bottom of the same unembedding ranking), the classic Voita suppression signature, so it does not prepare an upcoming token.

The pole fires on the bare word-piece tokens the tokenizer emits while a longer word is being spelled out from pieces: above all the opening piece of a word built on a classical stem (' con' in concomitant/conduction/confluence, ' contr' in contraindication/Contrary, ' const', ' constr', ' syn'/' Synt', ' synt', ' magnet' in magnetosphere/magnetometer, ' electr', ' therm', ' phot', 'onom') and interior pieces of the same kind ('atar' in cataract, 'olo' in apologetics, 'mon' in thermonuclear/monochromatic, 'lo' in xylophone). It stays near zero on short or common words and when the same content arrives as one token (hyphenated 'thermo-nuclear' drops from 5.4 to 1.1), and a given piece gives the same activation whether or not the word continues ('the con artist', 'con game' and 'concomitant' all fire the ' con' piece at 5.1-8.5), so it reacts to the piece already read, not to a topic or an upcoming token.

The pole fires on a token that continues an in-progress multi-token chunk: the predictable middle piece after its stem (Hay->ao, re->-ex->amine, began->to->decline, mean->I->think), and falls silent once the chunk completes. It is driven by the left-hand stem rather than token identity or the upcoming completion: the same surface token without its stem stays quiet, while swapping the next word changes nothing.

Qwen2.5-0.5B L21/N756+ fires on a word-internal sub-word fragment of a longer, non-lexicalised word: short letter-chunks with no leading space (' Am', ' am', ' em', ' Em', 'Ex', 'br', 'ij', ' sil', ' imp', ' aqu', ' Gre', 'astr') that begin or continue a rare name, foreign word or technical/Latinate term (Amro, Amish, amodiaquine, Rijksmuseum, silversmith, amperes, imparts, Extrême), predicting activity whenever such a fragment appears inside a multi-token word. The response is word-invariant once the fragment is fixed (' Am' = 7.3 before 'ro', 'ish', 'ato', 'ida' and 'her'; ' em' = 4.9 before 'itters', 'erald') and near zero when the same letters form a complete common word ('I am' 0.0-0.3), sit inside a single-token word ('Amsterdam', 'America', 'Amazing'), or when the passage is ordinary prose; a further 2-3x gain comes from the surrounding technical frame (identical 'at 90 amperes' scores 3.2 after 'The current was measured' but 0.3 after 'It was measured').

This neuron fires retrospectively on geometric concepts, mathematical curves, coordinate geometry, and graphical plotting terminology (such as 'angle', 'triangle', 'circle', 'curve', 'slope', 'vector', and plotting verbs). It remains inactive on non-geometric everyday nouns, abstract algebra, and non-mathematical senses of words.

Fires on a short subword fragment (typically a 2-4 character stem such as ' Fle', ' Ham', ' Mer', ' Trem', ' tre', 'ah', 'az', '.T', 'ED', or the first digit of a ZIP code) at the moment the text has started spelling out an unfamiliar surname, identifier, foreign all-caps word or code/number string that this token does not complete, so the model must still supply the rest of the unit; it is near-silent when the same characters form a complete familiar word or entity (' Ham' in 'West Ham', Danish ' tre', single-token names such as ' Smith', ' Hanks', ' Fleming') and much weaker on a later repeat of a name already spelled earlier in the context. Retrospective: its output uniformly promotes 'edge' tokens regardless of context and ablation changes the next-token distribution very little (KL ~0.005 at peaks), so it is not preparing the continuation.

Fires on the closing tag delimiter '</' when closing HTML or XML tags beginning with 'h' (especially heading elements <h1>–<h6>, <head>, <heading>, and <host>), and on apostrophes in French elision prefixes (such as j', d', and l'). While its output projection aligns with 'head'/'hand' vocabulary tokens preparing upcoming tag names, its direct causal KL is small, exhibiting retrospective tag-structure detection and occasional background activity on common n-grams like 'sat on'.

Retrospective detector of literal, vivid descriptions of physical scenes and bodies in motion. It fires on the concrete noun, or on the 'nearly/almost' + motion verb, when a natural object or body part does something physical: strongest on the literal word 'sun' (the sun came up/rose/set), then on things like branches pushing through a roof, eyebrows/heart 'nearly' touching or stopping, an eagle's wings 'and soared', waves 'crashed' on rocks, leaves 'rustled', and on 'fast' in the stock phrase 'X is fast approaching'. It stays near zero for the same words in non-physical, figurative or institutional use ('the band came up', 'Sun Microsystems', 'over the moon', 'raining cats and dogs', 'moving fast.', 'nearly finished the report') and on technical or administrative text; sporadic peaks on mid-word subword pieces of rare words (capecit|ab|ine, Gurt|ov|oy, Danish ' ø|konomien') are leftovers that this hypothesis does not predict.

The pole fires on clinical maternal-newborn-child-health writing: obstetric/perinatal passages (fetal/foetal, fetus, neonatal, congenital, gestational, prenatal/postnatal, intrapartum, postpartum, preeclampsia, placenta, umbilical, amniotic, Apgar, preterm birth, low birth weight, small-for-gestational-age, neonatal jaundice/sepsis, perinatal mortality) and child-health disease/deficiency statements (vitamin A or iodine deficiency, measles mortality, malnutrition), with strength rising as such clinical content accumulates. It is inactive on adult/general medicine (hypertension, cancer, diabetes, infections) and on lay or non-clinical text; ordinary proper names (Smith, Obama) do not fire, and the isolated strong peaks on the rare name-initial fragments ' V' (Vargas, Valesky) and ' W' (Waddell) are a separate token-level residue outside this reading.

This pole fires retrospectively when the current token is strongly constrained by its immediate left context: subword or digit fragments completing a multi-token word, number or abbreviation (Se->ine, 1->00, 5->p, Pl->ants), and the predictable filler of a local syntactic slot (a determiner after the preposition 'from', 'of' after a measure noun, the noun completing 'the ...', the verb continuing a subject). It stays near silent on tokens that begin a new phrase or topic, notably sentence-initial 'The' itself (mean strength 0.0), and its output direction strongly suppresses 'The'-initial next tokens, consistent with a mid-phrase continuation signal that votes against a sentence restart.

This pole sits at a low baseline over ordinary prose (peaks below ~0.7, predicted inactive) and is silenced to near zero at and just after conversion/transformation-domain tokens such as convert, conversion, transform, currency or exchange. It spikes sharply on the single space immediately before a numeral in the exact frame '<liquid> boils at <number>' with the numeral directly adjacent, strongest for sentence-initial 'Water boils at <number>' (peak near max ~3.7) and weaker for other liquids; insertions breaking adjacency (e.g. 'about') or non-initial subjects reduce it to weak/borderline.

N2135+ fires on the punctuation that closes a short label or headline at the start of a text: the colon of a speaker/label tag (line-initial 'Human:' peaks at 15.1, eight times the scan maximum; 'Assistant:' 2.4, 'Q:' 1.8, 'abstract:' 0.8) or the blank line that ends a bare name/headline ('Molly Henderson\n\n' 0.8), and on the line-initial token 'Human' itself (3.5). Ordinary prose, word labels ('Question:', 'User:', 'Note:'), and the same Q:/headline markers once four or more tokens of text precede them stay near zero (<=0.2), while the Human/Assistant tags keep firing at a reduced 4.0/0.9 in later turns.

This pole is a ' with'-token detector: it peaks on the token ' with' itself (nearly all of its activations above 1.0 are on ' with'; no other token family comes close), but only when the left context makes that 'with' a descriptive/attributive connector to a thing rather than a complement - i.e. when ' with' is immediately preceded (i) by a comma ('the engines, with each cylinder firing', 'the paper, with co-authors in Boston') or (ii) by an indefinite thing noun phrase 'a/an (adj) N' ('a loan with a high interest rate', 'an old bridge with a stone arch', 'a phone with a cracked screen'). It stays at baseline when 'with' is a verb/adjective complement or part of a fixed multiword preposition ('filled with', 'compatible with', 'along with', 'together with', 'dealt with'), when it follows a definite person, group, event or relational noun or a definite object NP without a comma ('the man with a beard', 'the team with the best record', 'a chat with a friend', 'the problem with the plan', 'the car with the flat tyre'), and in clause-initial 'With ...' ('With a loud crash, the door fell'); the same neuron's positive pole is instead a broad ' into' detector.

Fires on the word that names an industrial production site or sector: the head noun or adjective of 'factory/plant/mill/works/refinery/quarry/mine/industry/industrial/manufacturing/processor/blue-collar', strongest when the preceding modifier names a heavy-industry or commodity good (steel, cotton, sugar, garment, poultry processing, iron), as in 'steel industry', 'sugar mill', 'processing plant', 'Iron Works', 'industrial revolution'. It stays weak (<~25% of max) when the same word has a non-industrial sense (potted/flowering plant, pepper mill, complete works) or names a service sector (insurance, music, banking industry), and on generic production verbs like 'making'. It reacts to what has been read (retrospective) and does not prepare a specific next token.

The pole fires on the second, head part of a technical term written as one fused word: the object noun that closes a verb+object identifier (Set|Key, Load|Library, add|Class, set|RequestHeader, clear|Cache, add_library, import_module, To|Primitive, Start|Activity) and the stem of a fused prefixed technical word (de|ferences, anti|-western, Pan|-European, hypo|glyc|emic). It peaks when the two parts are written with no space between them and is usually well below the activity line (though not always zero) when a space separates them, while the same nouns as ordinary vocabulary ('the key is on the table', 'the service was slow'), noun-first or possessive compounds (camelCase, myKey, documentParser, ClassName, whiteSpace) and nonce strings (florbulateCache, SetBanana, camelKey) stay near zero.

L4/N2809+ fires on the continuation token of a multi-token written name or rare technical term in expository prose: the later element of a title-case proper name ('Hospital' in Children's Hospital, 'Men' in X-Men, 'Ones' in the Three Pure Ones, 'Consortium' in the ESMO European Consortium) or an interior piece of a rare word ('sth' in Kunsthistorisches, 'ication' in Claudication, 'ila' in Kapila, 'y' in Pompey). It is inactive on the first element of such a name, on the same words lowercased or used as ordinary common nouns, and on eating vocabulary (eat, food, meal, diet), which drives this same unit strongly negative.

The negative pole fires on the token that completes a stative, generic or passive predicate about an abstract, non-physical subject (a task, question, decision, action, problem, work, rule, price or quantity), typically built from a high-frequency general-purpose verb - do, make, take, answer, solve, apply, occur, happen, rise, be true, be forthcoming - as in 'no action was taken', 'little progress was made', 'the work is done', 'the question was answered', 'the problem was solved', 'no explanation was forthcoming', 'this is true of the iron cross', 'the same rules apply to everyone'. It stays near zero when the same predicate word takes a physical object or a specific event as subject ('the phone was answered', 'the dishes were done', 'the house was sold'), when the clause is active or agentive ('they took no action', 'he answered all the questions'), or when a lexically specific verb replaces the general one ('the work was sold', 'the decision was announced', 'the matter was resolved').

L4/N3740- fires on the token that closes a memorised multi-word frame: the fixed second element of a stock phrase or template whose identity is pinned by the preceding anchor word, not by the sentence. The strongest frames are conventional gender binomials ('him or her' 3.0, 'his or her' 2.6-3.1, 'men and women' 1.5-1.9, 'mothers and fathers' 1.5), then grammatical stock phrases ('so as to' 1.2-1.7, 'able to' 0.9-1.0, 'the fact that' 1.1, 'whether or not' 0.6, 'on the other hand' 0.7, 'once again' 1.9, 'in their own right' 1.8) and code/markup templates ('@+id' 1.7, '$_SESSION' 0.7-1.1, '<?xml', '____' 1.7); it is not a predictability, frequency or coordination detector, since equally probable continuations outside a memorised frame ('wanted to' 0.00, 'ready to' 0.07, 'yes or no' 0.13, 'own hands' 0.32, 'once more' 0.18) stay near zero and a merely conventional-but-specific pairing ('king and queen' 0.21) never reaches the collective-pair level.

This pole fires retrospectively when the current token completes a conventionalized local frame opened by preceding material: a comma closing a fronted adjunct ('far away, there lived') or a list-final item before its conjunction ('one egg, and'), or a complement selected by its head ('Once'+'upon', 'sat'+'on', 'import numpy'+'as', 'through'+weekday, 'ORDER BY'+column). Peak strength is set jointly by the head-plus-peak combination rather than either token alone, so swapping the head ('sat'->'waited') or the peak (','->'and'/'plus', 'upon'->'atop', weekday->'xyz') collapses firing while same-frame substitutions (Sunday->Monday) leave it unchanged.

Retrospective local phrase-completion detector: the pole fires on the token that completes a short-range chunk opened by the preceding one or two tokens — the second half of a fixed collocation (compared with, at least), a subword continuation (Se+ine, am+oxic), or a content word filling a slot set by a nearby function word (void because, hiked to, in O). The same surface token fires strongly with its opener present and weakly when the opener is swapped out.

L5/N1425+ fires on the punctuation token that closes a clause the text asserts in its own voice - the sentence-final '.' (including the hard line break of line-wrapped prose) and the ':' that introduces an apposition or specification ('looked at perspective-taking: the degree to which ...') - and its strength is passage-gated rather than set by the punctuation: a boundary is ~7x more likely to fire when the previous sentence boundary of the same passage fired (0.30 vs a 0.04 base rate), so 98% of '.' tokens sit near zero (mean -0.02) while every sentence-final period of a firing passage spikes to 0.7-1.8. At that identical closing position it collapses when the clause is reported from someone else ('The director said the clinic offers ...' 0.02 vs 'The director saw the clinic offers ...' 0.70), is enclosed in quotation marks, or closes a list item rather than a sentence - the negative pole takes over on the tokens just after a speech-reporting verb (' said' 0.38) - and the Jacobian-lens token list is incoherent (kurtosis 3.6, ' 


' / '/bower' / Chinese fragments), so no single upcoming token is prepared.

The negative pole tracks forward-looking time reference: it peaks where a clause places an event after the narrative present, either through an explicit future-time expression (' soon', ' shortly', ' imminent', ' coming', ' upcoming', ' next week/year/spring', ' in the near future', ' eventually', ' before long', ' any day now') or through a prospective predicate whose complement is still unrealized ('is set to', 'is due to', 'is expected to', 'is scheduled to/for', 'plans/intends to', 'is going to', 'is about to'). It returns to baseline when the same vocabulary describes past or completed events ('arrived soon after', 'was released in June', 'had expected to win', 'was about to leave'), present states or habituals ('leaves at six every morning'), present-tense epistemic complements ('is said/believed/reported/known to be'), and ordinary infinitival 'to' ('wants to leave'), while a bare 'will' plus a lexical verb with no explicit future-time expression is only a weak cue (typically 0.1-1.2 on the pole's 7.5 scan scale).

The pole fires retrospectively on the token that completes a conventional, highly predictable continuation of the preceding phrase: the current token is the canonical completion (idiom or collocation such as 'second half' and 'landed on', code syntax such as '):', a measure unit such as 'mg', or a recipe ingredient such as 'flour') licensed by several preceding tokens, so replacing the completion with an unpredictable token, or the licensing context with a non-licensing one holding the peak token fixed, collapses activation while changes after the peak leave it exactly unchanged.

Peaks retrospectively on the token that continues or completes a concrete quantity expression: a digit inside a multi-digit measurement, count, percentage, or year, a written number or frequency word (five, three, twice, one), or the of closing a measure phrase such as two cups of, when the local left context introduces a quantity (comparatives, by/at/to, or a preceding digit). Weak activation on unrelated content words (return, summit, void) is acknowledged leftover noise below half-max.

Fires on the verb token itself (its final subword) of transitive verbs whose direct object is a person whose knowledge, belief or holdings the subject changes: informing/reminding/warning/advising/alerting/telling, persuading/convincing/reassuring/begging, thanking/congratulating/accusing, and robbing/depriving (e.g. ' reminding', ' persuade', ' informing', ' convince', ' thank', ' rob', 'ive' in 'deprive'); strongest for the progressive or bare form after an auxiliary or connective ('is reminding', 'had to persuade', 'without first informing'). It is weak or silent on transitive verbs that act on a person without altering what they know or have (help, force, sway, bring, show, greet, praise, blame, allow), on the object and complement that follow, and on noun or adjective derivatives ('reminder', 'information', 'informed consent', 'persuasive').

Fires (retrospectively) on the token where someone's turn or response in an exchange is introduced or named: most strongly the opening quotation mark or colon that begins a quoted utterance right after a speech-act tag ("interrupted, “", "continued:", "interjected, “"), then reply/speech-act verbs in dialogue tags (answered, replied, insisted, suggested, asked, demanded; not non-speech tags like nodded, smiled, sighed) and nouns naming a chosen strategic response (move, switch, pick, choice, action, response, reply, counsel/defense), but not plain nouns like bill, plan, idea, trip or hire. A separate strong token-level offshoot: 'dominant' (and weaker 'recessive') as a mode of genetic inheritance ("autosomal dominant", "the gene is dominant"), plus 'no matter what'.

The negative pole fires on the verb (or its nominalisation) that names an institutional act of settling or putting something on the record - approve/approval, adopt, agree/agreed, ratify, endorse, confirm, announce/announcement, declare, define, specify/spec, disclose, file, allege, pass, sign - when the agent doing it is a corporate or collective body (a board, council, committee, commission, shareholders, officials, a company, a court, an API/type spec). The same verb falls to near zero when the agent is a private individual ('My sister approved the merger' = 0.12 vs 'The board approved the merger' = 4.63 of a 4.88 max), and institutional sentences whose verb withholds or merely considers (reject, veto, deny, review, consider, read) stay below the active threshold.

Fires on the OPENING delimiter of an inline markup span in prose or scientific text, i.e. the token that starts a Markdown/Pandoc formatted run glued to the following word: Pandoc subscript/superscript '~' and '^' (as in T~2~, (SurfO)~2~, 2^nd^), Markdown emphasis ' *' / ' _', fused italic tokens like '_N', '_O', '_the', and Apex '__' in '__c'; the matching closing delimiter stays near zero, the same characters used as ordinary punctuation or code identifiers (my_var, H_2O, -, =) do not fire, and activation is much stronger when the document has already used that kind of inline markup earlier (the second '~'/'^'/'_' opener beats the first, and bare ' _' italics barely fire without prior markup). Weaker leftovers (~0.3 of max) are other span-opening punctuation such as opening quotes, parenthetical dashes ' –', ' /' in '/CNW/' and a dateline comma.

Retrospectively detects references to a named, versioned artifact (software, spec, publication, hardware, or event edition), peaking on the release noun itself (version, edition, firmware, software, kernel) or on the digit/decimal suffix completing the identifier (e.g. version 1.5, Rails 3.0, MathML2, B12, Mach 2.04, Ninth Edition); identical digits after generic nouns (year 2016, price 2.04, dinner 1.5) stay near zero.

The pole fires where a clause says that a valued, needed thing is absent, denied, insufficient or being cut down, and peaks on that valued word or on the operator's complement: a negator or a reduction/removal word (no, not, without, cannot, lack of, not enough, less, little, insufficient, reduce, cut, lower, block, limit, restrict, minimize, deny) applied to a benefit, right, resource or capacity such as safety, water, jobs, rights, pay, health, freedom, prosperity, quality, motivation or absorption. It stays quiet when the same negator or reduction word applies to something unwanted ('reduce crime/poverty/costs/risks', 'no problems', 'not dangerous'), when the same valued noun sits under a neutral or supportive verb ('describe/measure/improve/protect the quality', 'increases prosperity'), and on bare intransitive decline ('profits fell').

The pole fires on the preposition that introduces the scope phrase of an abstract head noun: the pied-piped 'in which' (or 'by which' after 'means') of a manner or means noun — 'a way in which', 'the ways in which', 'the manner in which', 'the means by which', strongest for plural 'ways' and indefinite 'a way' — and the period preposition 'in', 'for', 'during' or 'since' after an ordinal time noun ('the first time in years', 'the only time in the series', 'the best possible time during your stay'). It is inactive on the same prepositions after concrete or locative heads ('the house/world/case in which'), on links that are not pied-piped relatives ('the way that', 'a way of doing', 'a way to do'), on a time word without an ordinal ('in the morning', 'the time in which'), and on the agent of an ordinary action passive ('served by the landlord'); the scan's 'widely seen/viewed by' peaks are an unexplained leftover.

The negative pole fires, retrospectively, on the token that completes a memorised multi-token string belonging to a technical artefact: the second element of a fixed legal/technical expression ('notice of', 'Request for', 'CHANGE MASTER', 'Chem. Eur.', 'further notice') or of a known identifier or log label ('com.intellij.openapi.vfs.Virtual|File', 'Page|Reference', 'Job|Context', 'debug1:'), i.e. the position where one or two left-hand tokens plus a stored string already fix the token's identity. It is not a syntax, register or next-token-probability detector: the identical surface token elsewhere is silent (' of' occurs 3,422 times in the scan and exceeds 0.5 only three times, all 'notice/notified of'; 'Content-Type:', 'SQLSTATE', 'Fatal Protocol Error' and 'House of Representatives' stay under 0.25), while swapping the anchor word ('notice'->'note', 'Request'->'demand', 'debug1'->'Debug1', 'Chem. Eur.'->'Chem. Biol.', 'JobContext'->'ItemBucket') or the identifier's memorised prefix sharply reduces the response (2.21->0.12, 1.94->0.30, 1.75->0.12, 1.42->0.22, 1.65->0.73, 1.15->0.55).

N2159+ is a graded-comparison detector: it fires where a quantity or degree is modified rather than stated flatly, and its sharpest peak is the second element of a reduplicated comparative ('worse and worse' 2.37, 'less and less' 1.99, 'wider and wider' 1.94, 'steeper and steeper' 1.87, 'fewer and fewer' 1.79, 'more and more of a threat' 1.64) or the junction that closes such a phrase ('the plan costs less money and takes time' peaks on 'and' at 1.81, while the same clause with 'some money' gives 0.23; 'awareness has increased only recently' peaks on 'only' at 1.90), with a weaker word-level response to the ratio and contrast markers that carry a relation themselves ('per' 0.46 and 'per cent'/'percent'/'%' 0.36-0.42 mean vs 0.06 for an average scanned token; 'rather' 0.35, 'means' 0.25, 'while' 0.24, 'yet' 0.24). It is flat on single unmodified comparatives ('buying less every year' 0.36, 'rising much faster every year' 0.09, 'more accurate than the older version' 0.22), on non-comparative reduplication ('again and again' 0.04), and on ungraded factual prose and its topic words ('university' 0.03, 'scientists' 0.03, 'said' 0.03 as preceding context), so the peak is a retrospective response to the scalar phrase it sits in, not a preparation of a specific upcoming token (zeroing the pole moves almost no probability mass: KL 5e-5, top-10 concentration 0.39, and its output direction is near-Gaussian, Jacobian kurtosis 3.7, with a below-median output norm).

Retrospective detector of a possessive determiner (' their', ' his', ' her', ' our', ' your', ' my', ' its') that heads a noun phrase inside a prepositional phrase governed by the predicate - 'sent the toys to their teacher' (3.4), 'spoke with his advisors' (3.4), 'proud of their findings' (1.0), 'the sustainability of their farms' (2.9) - and it tracks that frame rather than the token: the same determiner as the verb's direct or indirect object ('sent their teacher all the toys', 0.2 vs 3.4), inside a subject-modifying or fronted PP ('To their teacher, the children gave the toys', 0.2), or an article or object pronoun in the same PP slot ('to the teacher' 0.4, 'to them' 0.1) stays near zero. Inside the PP frame the strength is graded by person/number agreement with the salient antecedent (plural subject: ' their' 3.4-4.4 vs ' his' 0.6-1.0; singular subject: ' his' 3.4 vs ' their' 1.5).

Fires on the token that seals a locally complete 2-4 word chunk: either the complement that saturates a preceding determiner, preposition, verb or frequent collocation (the onions, at sea, stock market, are you going), or the boundary token right after a finished clause or noun phrase (after, before, for, sentence-final period over a comma). It is driven by the 1-2 preceding tokens, so the same word fires weakly or not at all when the chunk is still open, incomplete, or continues.

The pole fires on a mention of the counterpart of a party already established in the passage: the second or other member of a named pair ("another material" after one material, "a second material", "the other material"), the second of two compared or contrasted parties ("For men" after women, "Group B" after Group A, "for Defendant" after Plaintiff), or a dual/plural anaphor collecting the named pair ("In both of them", "In both materials"). It stays near zero for first mentions with no counterpart, for repeated or unrelated substitute referents, and for two parties acting jointly or in agreement, whose mutuality vocabulary (mutual, agreement, relationship, cooperation) its negative output suppresses.

The pole fires on the first token of the word that continues a specific, individuated noun phrase: the head of a name-noun or technical noun-noun compound ('Hawaii residents' 1.27, 'company chief' 1.25, 'stent lumens' 2.14, 'CAMC's core' 2.52) or the copula/preposition that opens that noun's predicate ('this tune is' 2.05, 'the report of the committee was' 0.55, 'the game with' 1.97). It stays near zero when the same slot holds a generic qualifier ('local residents' 0.00, 'Nearby residents' 0.19, 'CAMC's good values' 0.32) or a clause-opening relativizer/coordinator ('the report that the committee...' 0.10, 'Hawaii and residents' 0.16), so neither the trigger-token list nor 'fires after any noun' predicts it.

This pole fires on the completion token of a conventional adjacent two-part unit begun by the immediately preceding token: an attributive or nominal collocation (income tax, smaller fee, growth rate), a verb-object idiom (take charge), or a quantity-plus-unit (two hours, 70 °C). The same peak token after an unrelated word, or with the unit broken, activates weakly or not at all.

Layer-1 lexical detector for a small closed set of high-frequency, space-prefixed 'light' modifier words: above all ' still', ' able', ' little', ' how' and ' soon', more weakly ' willing' and ' alive'. It peaks when that word fills a clause-medial modifier/complement slot right after a light function word ('was still', 'be able to', 'a little', 'is how ...', 'as soon as'), is about 4x weaker when the same word follows a content word instead ('the problem still remains' 0.24 vs 'the problem was still there' 1.07), and is near zero on near-synonyms (already, bit, glad, when, early), on capitalized/other token variants, and on the same letters inside a longer word. The word that follows it does not change the response.

Fires when the current clause describes or performs a solicitation — someone appealing, urging, asking, begging, pleading, fundraising, or posting to request help, money, action, or information, in any language and including nouns like fundraiser, wallet, or folded hands in a plea context; neutral reports, descriptions, or incidental mentions of the same objects without a request do not activate it.

This pole fires on tokens that spell out a clock time or a time/date format pattern: the digit-and-separator pieces of 11:56:34, 08:45, 00:30:00 and 2018-08-29T11:56:34Z, the pattern pieces of HH:mm:ss, %H:%M, dd/MM/yyyy and d MMM y HH:mm:ss, and the same time expression spelled in words (nine fifteen, ten forty-five, hour minute). It sits at zero on narrative prose, on sentences that mention a time or date without spelling a value, and on non-temporal literals such as version numbers (3.14.2), dates with no clock component (2026-11-06, 29/08/2018), quantities with units and long opaque identifiers (UUIDs, hex digests, URLs, file paths).

The pole is a clause/sentence-boundary detector: it is predicted active on the token that closes a clause, sentence or text line - final . ! ? : ; ..., merged punctuation such as '."', ').' and '...\n', the non-Latin terminators । and 。, and segment-ending line breaks - and, more weakly, on a clause-linking conjunction immediately after such a boundary (' but', ' and', ' since', ' because'). It is predicted inactive on the same punctuation used inside a phrase (decimal points, abbreviations like 'Dr.', URL dots, list commas) and on phrasal coordination, where the token carries no boundary.

This pole fires retrospectively when a person's occupational title, office, credential, or party affiliation appears in a name-identifying appositive or copular construction (e.g. 'Newman, who is the chairman', 'Train, a police regional director, said', 'Sanders (I-VT)'), peaking on the role noun itself or on the determiner introducing a multi-word title; the same nouns used generically or of someone other than the named person activate it much less.

The pole fires at the period that ends a self-contained statement in connected, article-style prose (news, feature, blog or essay writing), most strongly at a line/paragraph-final period and when the sentence closes a direct quotation or an attributed claim ('...," writes/says X', 'according to Y'). It is near zero at punctuation inside a sentence, inside quotation bodies, and at sentence ends in reference, list, manual or bibliographic text, and its output write suppresses end-of-document and boilerplate tokens rather than promoting a specific next token.

The pole fires at the token where a sentence commits to a proposition it presents as information: the copula or evidential predicate after an abstract claim/information subject (“the fact/truth/reality/claim/rumour/hypothesis/assumption/premise/implication/bottom line/point/reason/conclusion/result/situation is/was/remains”, and “the news/evidence/report/statement/view/opinion is that …”, where the peak lands on the complementizer “that”), or the reporting/evidential verb whose subject is an information source (“the report/newspaper/magazine/press/study/research/data/figures/polls/survey/census/memo/rules/law/contract/court/government reports/reported/states/says/shows/reveals/indicates/suggests/concludes/claims/notes/adds/confirms/announced/found/ruled”). It is retrospective — the peak is fixed once its prefix is read and no continuation changes it — and it stays quiet on direct predication about concrete objects, events or physical properties (“the car is red”, “the report was long and boring”, “the ministry is closed on Monday”), on personal or first-person opinion verbs (“I think”, “the girl says that …”, “the witness reported that …”), and on non-assertive uses of the same words (“he reports to the manager”, “the bell indicates the end of class”).

This pole fires on scalar-closure degree constructions: a comparative or additive degree word (better, worse, further, even, only, nor, all after a superlative) that ranks, extends, or exhausts a scale relative to prior discourse, licensed by an exhaustive operator such as negation (no/nor/other), additive focus (even), restrictive focus (only), or a universal (all). Bare comparatives without such a licensor, and the same function words in non-scalar uses, do not activate it; its output direction suppresses redundant further/more-family continuations.

L19/N4304-negative is a retrospective lexical detector: it fires on individual word tokens that carry register-specific, non-core vocabulary, i.e. the fixed vocabulary of a specialised domain or marked usage (sexual/adult terms such as kiss, sexual, erotic, libido, intimate, pleasure; technical, chemical and medical terms such as methyl, ethyl, olefin, hydroxyl, vascular, somatic, receptor, estrogen, lipid, and legal-administrative terms such as licensed, authorization, concession, trespass, indict, exempt), and it sits at zero on register-general English, i.e. function words, basic nouns and verbs (water, dog, table, food, walk), basic emotion words (anger, fear, shame, pain) and academic words used across every register (analysis, theory, method, science, cognitive, search, logic, array). The response is carried by the token itself rather than by its topic or its predictability: swapping only the word moves the peak by 0.53-0.82 of max activation, whereas rewriting the whole surrounding sentence around the same word moves it by at most 0.03.

This pole is a retrospective detector for a 'Tro'/'tro' word onset at the current position: it fires on whole tokens spelling Tro-words ('Troy', 'Trojan', 'troll', 'trolling'), on subword onset pieces (' tro', ' Tro', ' Tr', ' T'/'t', Cyrillic ' тр', Greek ' τρ') and on their within-word continuations ('roy', 'j', 'rolling', 'ans'), but not on the same continuations without the onset ('rolling', 'Roy', 'toll') nor on other tr-initial or mid-word -tr- tokens ('truck', 'traffic', 'treat', 'control', 'street'). Its gain is set by the immediate left context, strongest after determiners/prepositions ('the', 'to', 'of', 'from') and weakest after verbs like 'say'/'found', but the onset-trigger requirement itself is strict.

This pole is a retrospective detector for the aspirated-b consonant pair 'bh' (a 'b'/'B' immediately followed by 'h') in rare, non-native words. It peaks at the sub-word token carrying the 'h': the pair may straddle a token boundary ('Ab'|'hay' 15.2, 'V'|'ib'|'hu' 8.9, 'b'|'hang' 8.9, 'B'|'hop' 7.6, Hindi भारत 'bhārat' 9.9) or sit inside one ('ĠBh' fires at the identical 3.56 in Bhutan, Bhishma, Bhakti and Bhavan); it also fires one step weaker (1-8) on the h-bearing word-internal fragment of other rare or foreign words (Bischoffsgemälde 'cho' 7.9, Brihadaranyaka 'had' 4.8, Hsiang 'ang' 4.2, Verhängen 'äng' 3.4), while every other consonant+h pair is an order of magnitude weaker (gh 1.3, vh 1.7, kh 0.5, ch/dh/sh/th/ph/wh/zh < 0.1), a fragment without 'h' stays near zero, and the strength is fixed by the left context (changing the words after the peak leaves the value bit-identical).

The pole fires on the digit tokens of a date reference to a year in 1000-1999: it peaks on the '9' of a 1900s year ('in 1989', 'of 1964', 'Oct. 15, 1903', '(1928-2014)', 'the 1920s', 'the 19th century'), fires less strongly on the '1' that opens any such year, and stays near zero for 2000s years ('In 2019'), for the same digits used as a bare count or label ('19 people', '1932 seats', 'Room 1932'), and for '19' inside a longer numeral. Its strength tracks how strongly the passage reads as a dated factual chronicle - the same year fires about 4 in a neutral sentence but about 18 after a natural-hazard or disruption statement ('Solar storms can damage power grids ... In 1989') - with weaker (2-6) responses to version strings and long digit IDs, and one top example ('not only you but your family also') left unexplained.

The pole fires at the word that introduces a span or point of time - the determiner or preposition just before it (' the', ' this', ' my', ' his', ' on'), or its first subword when there is none ('zaterdag', 'OCTOBER', 'Nisan', '250th', '今年') - whenever the context so far makes what follows a period of time rather than a thing: 'the entire afternoon', 'the whole night', 'the following week', 'the previous December', 'this morning', 'his 14th birthday', a date, day, month, holiday, or a date-format field in calendar code. It stays at its floor where the same determiner introduces an object, even with the same adjective and the same token count ('The rain continued the entire afternoon' 11.5 vs 'The rain flooded the entire valley' 0.9; 'The storm raged the entire night' 6.9 vs 'The storm flooded the entire old street' 0.1), so what decides it is the verb or preposition before the determiner, not the determiner, the adjective or the word after it.

L25/N292+ fires on tokens that sit inside a recalled, conventionally-fixed multi-token string — product and version identifiers ('Windows Server 2008 Enterprise', 'Windows NT 4.0', 'MOSS 2007'), acronyms introduced by their expansion ('Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC)', 'U.S.'), chemical/technical notation ('H_2SO_4', 'P-GP'), licence and code-doc boilerplate (' * For the full copyright ...', '@author', '// Purpose:') and multi-word title/product names ('Harry Potter and the ...') — where the wording is pulled from memory or from a naming/formatting convention rather than composed, so the model's next token is usually pinned down (median next-token entropy 0.9 nats at peaks vs 2.0 nats at matched positions, top-1 usually the actual continuation). Ordinary narrative prose and everyday collocations ('New York City', 'World War II', 'on the other hand' all stay under 0.4) leave it near zero, and its negative pole fires inside rare unfamiliar words ('phosphoglycolipid', 'Khmelnytskyi', 'triacylglycerol') where nothing is recalled.

The pole fires on a token that spells, or mid-word continues, a personal name in its Spanish or Portuguese form - strongest on common Iberian masculine given names (Juan, Luis, Miguel, Jose, Pedro, Rafael, Joaquin, Manuel, Rui, Joao) - in English or Spanish surrounding text and in any capitalization, e.g. 'uis' in 'Luis' and 'quin' in 'Joaquin'. It sits at baseline for names whose spelling is shared with English (John, David, Daniel) and for English words carrying the same subword pieces (quin in 'mannequin'), and is much weaker on Spanish common nouns, surnames and place names (casa, pesos, Ramos, Madrid); a few equally Spanish-looking names (Javier, Diego, Jesus) also stay near baseline, so apply the graded rule 'how Spanish-only the name is', not the language of the sentence.

Predicted active: the head token of a noun phrase that names a mathematical result or statement (theorem, lemma, inequality, principle, law, test, limit, formula) used as a term of art, with activity building over the words that lead into the term and peaking on that head (e.g. 'theorem' in 'the mean value theorem' ~16, 'numbers' in 'the law of large numbers' ~15, 'test' in 'the ratio test' ~8, 'inequality' in 'the triangle inequality' ~6), and usually falling back to the noise floor on the next word. Predicted inactive: ordinary prose, non-mathematical senses of the same words ('the law was passed', 'social inequality', 'she passed the test easily', all <=0.6), and mathematical objects that are not result words ('function', 'matrix', 'equation', 'transform'), which stay at the 0.1-0.4 noise floor.

N1471+ is a sparse retrospective detector of referential nominal terms in formal or specialist discourse: it peaks on the head token of a name or term once the preceding words complete it - institution/title names ('American Association', 'the Ministry of Shipping', 'Director-General'), technical and substance names ('D-dimer', 'IGF-II', 'hyaline membrane', 'sampling technique'), doctrinal or esoteric concepts ('spiritual/divine/sacred/hidden knowledge', 'wisdom'), and formal legal-social relations ('express written permission', 'pledged allegiance'). The same nouns stay quiet in generic or descriptive frames ('the local association', 'the amount of water', 'scientific knowledge'), and the negative pole instead fires on abstract property/process nominalisations ('quality', 'assessment', 'configuration', 'policy', 'management'); the pole's output direction promotes end-of-line punctuation while suppressing that nominalisation vocabulary.

This pole fires on astrobiology and planetary-science text - passages about water, ice, oceans, atmospheres, habitable conditions, or the search for life and biosignatures on other worlds - and it peaks on the token that carries that content (' water', ' ice', ' ocean', ' life', ' habitable', ' rivers'). The same words in everyday, terrestrial, molecular-biology, engineering or political contexts leave it near zero (measured peaks: 'On Mars, scientists found water' = 13.9 vs 'In Peru, scientists found water' = 1.2, 'The enzyme catalyses...' = 0.3), though a bare science-discovery sentence about water ('Scientists found water.') still gives a partial response (~10).

This pole is a retrospective token-identity detector for a narrow memorized subset of current tokens (including rain, hail, sunrise, sunshine, thunder, revenue, pinch, stared, triangle, noon, midnight, Sunday); it peaks on the matching token itself and drops to near zero on close semantic or single-letter neighbors such as snow, income, punch, square, Monday, or dog.

Fires on the second word of a conventionalized two-word commercial/consumer compound (credit/debit card(s), savings account, cell/mobile phone, phone number/call(s), PayPal, customer/insurance service terms), with most activation driven by the preceding modifier token; the same head noun alone or with a non-commercial modifier activates it only weakly.

A layer-0 unigram detector: the pole fires on the token itself, almost independently of context (85% of the integrated-gradient attribution sits on the peak token, 88-100% per example, only 1% on the preceding token; token identity explains 95% of the scan variance and position 0.06%), on a fixed cluster of mid-frequency written-English token embeddings centred on exercised control and efficacy rather than on a semantic class of meanings. Strength is graded and stable per surface form: highest (0.6-1.0 of the 2.40 scan max) on ' control'/' Control'/' controls'/' controlled'/' contro'/' uncontrolled' (1.7-2.2), ' effective'/' effectively'/' effectiveness'/' efficient'/' efficiently' (1.2-2.0), ' regulate'/' regulation'/' regulations'/' regulatory' (0.7-2.0), ' succeed'/' succeeded'/' successful'/' successfully'/'successor' (0.9-2.4), ' improve'/'improved'/'improving'/'improvement' (0.6-1.0), ' approved'/' authorized'/' audit'/' audits'/' comply' (0.8-1.2), ' eliminate'/'eliminated'/'erad'/'minimize'/' minimizing'/'maximize'/'optimized'/'optimal' (0.9-1.5), ' compete'/'competition'/'competitive'/'profit'/'profits'/'profitable'/'cooperate' (0.9-1.5), the calendar-date numeral tokens ' 1990'/'2000'/' 2000'/'1998'/' 1998'/'1999'/' 1996'/' 1988'/' 1980'-' 2004'/' Dec'/' December'/' Oct' (0.8-2.1, but ' 2018' reads 0.00 and ' 2010' 0.34), and the capitalised abbreviations or word-initial fragments of that register ('Comp'/' Comp'/' comp', 'Rec'/' rec', 'Reg', 'Impro', 'Micro', 'Motor', 'Machine', 'Robot', 'FDA', 'EC', 'NC'). A weaker band (0.25-0.6 of max) covers the rest of the management/technical vocabulary (' facilitate', ' implement'/'implemented'/'Implementation', ' establishing'/'establishment', ' coordinated'/'coordinating'/'coordination', ' modify'/'modified', ' utilized', ' refined', ' funded', ' promote', ' enhanced', ' influence'/'influenced', ' sustainable'/'sustainability', ' criminal'/'criminals', ' illegal'/'illegally', ' convict', ' ethical', ' Conservation', ' Forestry', ' wastewater', ' molecular', ' metabolic', ' amino', ' synthetic'), while it reads ~0 (below 0.1 of max) on ordinary vocabulary and on these semantically close non-members: ' support', ' health', ' safety', ' public', ' power', ' authority', ' management', ' development', ' integration', ' system'/'systems', ' program'/'programs', ' service'/'services', ' effects', ' drugs', ' companies', ' Congress', ' Senate', ' government', ' medical', ' water', ' food', ' children', ' cost'/'costs', ' investment', ' work'. Because member forms such as ' succeeded' (the scan maximum), ' cooperate', ' uncontrolled', ' minimizing', ' Fisheries', ' Implementation' and ' comply' occur too rarely to enter the scan's count>=3 top-token list, the claim is the word families and their documented strengths, not the top-200 token ids.

Fires retrospectively on evaluative, affectively valenced content words expressing a positive or negative emotion, value judgment, or charged appraisal (e.g. wonderful, disastrous, happily, lucrative, battle, struggle), regardless of polarity; does not fire on neutral descriptive, temporal, or function words.

The pole fires on tokens of the visual-arts and art-history lexicon: artwork and art-practice words (art, artist, artistic, arts, painting(s), sculpture/sculptural, gallery, museum, exhibition, curator, fresco, masterpiece), the period- and style-name vocabulary that frames them (Renaissance, Gothic, Byzantine, classical, contemporary, modern, Romantic, Victorian, medieval, antiquity, century/centuries), and the refined-taste register (elegance, exquisite, refinement, sophistication, luxury, decor, style, designer, palace, couture, ballet, theatre, opera), with the peak sitting on the triggering token itself rather than before it. It is silent on words that merely contain 'art' (artifact, article, artery, artificial), on music, film and fashion as such, and on everyday, sport, science and code vocabulary; a minor share of firings on bare Romance-diacritic pieces (e, ee, c-cedilla, n-tilde, a-circumflex in French words and names such as Rene) is a token-embedding neighbour of the same direction, not a second meaning.

Retrospective lexical detector at layer 1: the pole fires on the current token itself (86% of the input attribution sits on it; the same word peaks the same amount to within ~0.2 of scale whatever precedes it and at any position >= 1, and no token fires at position 0) when that token is a rare, specific word - a long-tail proper name (' Scotland' 0.92, ' Stockholm' 1.83, ' Sheffield' 0.84 on its 'ffield' piece, ' Liverpool' 1.17), a rare concrete noun (' magnet' 1.47, ' flour' 1.37, ' pumpkin' 1.27, ' butter' 1.07, ' Lyon' 0.79) or the stem/fragment of a rare technical word (' adren-' 1.92, ' cytok-' 1.79, ' cortisol' 1.53, ' neuron' 1.23, ' syn-' 1.52). It sits at the GELU floor (-0.17) on high-frequency vocabulary - function words, generic nouns (' city' -0.17, ' country' -0.17, ' water' -0.14, ' school' -0.16, ' market' -0.15), abstract nouns (' method' -0.17, ' system' -0.15, ' process' -0.16, ' factor' -0.16) and famous proper names (' Paris' -0.13, ' London' -0.11, ' China' -0.06, ' America' -0.15) - and roughly 80% of even rare words stay at the floor (' valley' +0.04, ' needle' +0.04, ' stream' +0.01, ' enormous' -0.15, ' antiquated' -0.11), so this is a graded long-tail detector rather than a switch on all rare tokens; the negative pole is only GELU's dip and carries no separate content.

This pole fires on structural punctuation inside a formal constructed expression: commas separating listed items (function arguments, array dimensions, SQL column lists), opening brackets starting argument or index lists, dots joining dotted attribute chains, and terminal marks closing markup-embedded phrases. The same characters in plain prose stay silent: commas after 'Paris' or '1969' and sentence-final dots score 0, a semicolon substituted into a code-comma slot scores 0, and the identical 'Hello, world!' string fires only inside its HTML frame.

Fires retrospectively on the token that completes a conventional multi-word proper name (country, court, league, newspaper, legislative body, event, agency, or initialism) when it directly continues the name's standard capitalized first half, e.g. States after United, Court after Supreme, Ireland after Northern, League after Major, Times after New York, Commons after House of, Series after World, Works after Public. The same head noun with a wrong modifier, in lowercase, or in a novel capitalized bigram does not activate it.

Retrospective current-token detector: the pole peaks on the token being read when that token is a lexical content word from its preferred memorized subset (e.g. light, galaxy, Armstrong, function, central, asked, March, cups, time, open, final, brown, called, war, bread, black, peace, reason; graded 0.1-0.9), while staying near zero on closed-class function words, punctuation, subword continuations, and most other content words (lion, green, night, love, window) even in identical slots; preferred-token amplitude is scaled up to ~2x by supportive left context (billion boosts light 0.33 to 0.90), and every text's first token fires a content-blind floor (~0.2-0.5) that carries no signal.

This pole fires retrospectively on operational and organizational vocabulary of formal expository prose, words for attempting, using, structuring, choosing, and judging feasibility (attempt/attempted, serve/serves/serving, employ, facilitate, feasible, practicable, opportunity, advantage, ranging, comprising, preferably, eventually, volition, albeit, thereby), including subword pieces of technical terms and news-era proper names (Gabbard, Ferenc, Interwar-Inter, KIND, INTERRUPTION). It stays near-inactive on everyday concrete nouns, casual or epistemic adverbs, emotional, moral-evaluative or social-interaction words, agentive -er nouns, and concrete institutional nouns (dog, quickly, probably, deserves, possible, community, despair, server, tribunal).

This pole fires retrospectively on the head-noun token that completes a short determiner / quantifier / numeral / adjective / noun-modifier + noun phrase (e.g. 'last year', 'three times', 'stock market', '100 degrees'). The same noun preceded by a verb, conjunction, or other non-licensing token fires weakly, while changes to distant words or to the token after the peak leave the peak unchanged.

N2748+ is a retrospective token-identity detector, not a context or next-token feature: the peak sits on the word at the current position (zeroing layer 1's attention output leaves 60-90% of it, and the same word shifts by well under a third across different preceding and following text), near neighbours of a firing word also fire (their mean is 0.17 against 0.01 for the vocabulary at large), and the rest of the vocabulary sits at 0. It fires on a broad, graded, lexically specific set of everyday content words centred on three clusters - commerce and media nouns (firm, firms, brand, brands, market, markets, shares, ownership, ads, commercials, logo, auction, wholesale, publisher, studio, news, press), consumer-goods nouns (diaper, diapers, pants, jeans, trousers, shoes, stove, underwear) and evaluative degree adverbs (exclusively, constantly, increasingly, suddenly, rightfully, firmly, forcefully, entirely, continually, actively, totally, completely) - and it stays silent on function words, on abstract or technical Latinate vocabulary (method, process, analysis, system, information), on neutral objects, places and organisations (water, house, car, road, tree, city, school, company, group, product, report, retail) and on manner and hedging adverbs (quickly, carefully, probably, generally, apparently); the boundary is lexical rather than conceptual, so exact word form and case decide the outcome - 'firm' 0.80 vs 'group' 0.00 and 'Falls' 0.69 vs 'falls' 0.02 in the same sentence, 'exclusively' 0.60 vs 'solely' 0.00 - and a new word should be labelled predicted-active only when it falls inside those three neighbourhoods.

Retrospective chunk-completion detector for low-frequency technical multi-token units: it fires on the token that completes the unit, either a no-space final subword of a split jargon word (pum-ice, cytotox-ic, l-umen, long-term) or the second word of a conventional technical collocation (liquid solution, predicting future, document handling), when the preceding stem and wider domain frame predict that completion; the identical surface token in an everyday word or generic frame (coward-ice, the solution, the future) stays near silent.

This pole fires retrospectively on a token that completes a familiar two-token phrase or name already begun in the text, such as the second half of Timmy, a polite reply such as yes please, or a common verb phrase, regardless of the specific phrase. It does not fire on the first token of such a phrase, or on novel tokens that do not complete a familiar unit.

Retrospective detector for a specific learned lexical set on the current token: BPE fragments isolating the ph digraph (oph, ph, roph); any inflection of the verb lemmas EXPRESS, REFLECT, CATCH, CONTAIN; locative -where adverbs graded somewhere > anywhere > everywhere > nowhere; the prepositions among/amidst and predicative worth; and Old-World continent adjectives (Asian, African, European). It does not fire on near-synonyms outside these lemmas (stated, taught, deflect, between, including, Martian), other ph-spellings (phone, photo, trophy), or other fragments (obe, obia).

This pole fires on the token that completes a predictable two-part unit begun in the preceding one or two tokens: the second piece of a multi-token word (Att+ending, special+ising, downs+ides, Wi+Fi, Vigil+ance), the second word of a fixed compound, collocation or title (traffic+stop, cell+phone, Love+Music, Festivals+&), or a participle/infinitive completing a periphrastic verb form ('re+driving, to+stop). The same surface token preceded by an unrelated word activates substantially less, and the first piece alone does not activate it.

The pole fires on GPT-2's byte-level pieces of non-Latin-script text: partial UTF-8 fragments such as 'の�' (a kana plus the lead byte of the next kanji), lone Greek bytes 0xCE/0xCF and their continuation bytes, mojibake and Japanese/Chinese script fragments, and it fires on nearly every token of running Greek text. It also fires, more weakly and only in some contexts, on a fixed set of non-standalone English word pieces, foreign function words and code identifiers ('surv-', 'traject-', '-ination', ' et', ' alt', 'Label', 'func', 'href'), while ordinary English prose, digits and punctuation hold it at its GELU floor (about -0.17), as mostly do Cyrillic, Arabic and Hebrew text.

Fires on the lowercase, space-prefixed word-start token ' rest' in any sense ('the rest (of)', the verb or noun 'rest', 'rest area', and as the first piece of Spanish 'resta' or 'restorative'), at about 0.5-0.95 of max and strongest after 'the'; a smaller set of word-start pieces of abstract or Latinate words fires at about 0.4-0.95: ' mis' (French 'mis', English 'mis-'), ' complement', ' traject', ' evolution', ' ownership', ' ev' (of 'evocative'), ' gen' (of 'genotypes'), plus a LaTeX '{' right after \frac or \mathrm. It stays below about 0.25 of max on tokens that only contain 'rest' ('Rest' capitalised, ' restaurant', ' arrest', ' rested', ' restoration', ' restart'), on synonyms (' end', ' head', ' sleep', ' sit', ' others', ' members'), and on ordinary function words and concrete nouns, though some other abstract nouns (' remainder', ' whole', ' history', ' concept', ' relativity', ' gravity') reach about 0.3.

Ignoring each text's first token (where it has a floor), this pole is a retrospective lexical detector: it fires on the current token at 0.4-1.5x the scan scale when the token is a common word of public/collective life, work and media (care, health, staff, press, media, art, land, train, protest, benefit, rights, energy, value, program, result, war, team, population, 'thing'), a light transfer/exchange or motion verb (give/gave/given/gives, sell/sold, offer, hold/held, go/went/going, come, bring, want, help), or one of the very common quantifier/discourse words (not, most, any, least, still, ever, never, good, best, sure), and it fires more weakly (0.15-0.4x) on the rest of that same general vocabulary (city, council, authority, mayor, vote, law, news, power, radio, plan, women, man, take, put, keep, public, police). It sits at the GELU floor (0.00 of scale) on personal, domestic and natural-kind vocabulary (father, mother, child, family, friend, house, tree, table, cup, doctor, bird, cat, dog, book, garden, village), on perception, cognition and manipulation verbs (see, hear, watch, touch, follow, lead, leave, own, open, close, change, grow, clean, cut, fill, drop, lift, pull, build, sort, mix, count, arrange, remember, measure, save, buy, pay), and on longer abstract or institutional labels (society, community, culture, method, system, process, contract, economy, business, industry, history, question, court, minister, policy, budget, report, statement, paper); the split is lexical and graded rather than syntactic or sense-based, so 'give' fires while 'see' does not, 'sell' fires while 'buy' does not, and 'staff' fires while 'doctor' does not.

Fires at a linker or relational word (' and'/' or'/','/'('/' as'/' on'/kinship noun) when the preceding clause has introduced one person inside a pairing or attribution frame (co-stars, twins, parents, children, character name, spouse/daughter, opponent, role), preparing the upcoming proper-name token that completes the pair or apposition.

The pole retrospectively detects the token that opens a reference to a specific, already-individuated (normally animate) entity in English running prose: the possessive determiners (his, her, my, your, their, our, whose), the nominative personal pronouns (he, she, I, we, they, you, who), the possessive clitic 's, and the word-initial token of a personal or place name (Har- in Harland, Nor- in Norah, Ph- in Phyllis, Col-, San, Est-). It sits at its floor on bare articles, demonstratives, inanimate and accusative forms (the, a, this, that, its, which, it, him, them), and it roughly doubles when the same opener is the second or later element of a parallel or list construction ('his tuition ... and his books', 'his paternal lineage ... and his maternal lineage', the third name in a comma list).

The pole fires on formal, third-person descriptive/reference prose that states specific facts about a named subject - an encyclopedic or news sentence carrying that subject's date, category, nationality, role or creator ('X is a 1980 novel by American author Y', 'designed by the Swiss architect Robert Maillart', 'with the Carnegie Mellon University Press', 'U.S. News & World Report'). Its peaks are the determiners, dates and attribution words inside that descriptive predicate, and it sits at zero on conversation, plain narrative, code, procedural instructions, generic definitions ('A novel is a long work of fiction') and trivially known statements ('Paris is the capital of France').

The pole is a concreteness detector: it fires on the content words of clauses that describe physical, perceptible things and their properties - objects, materials and substances (stone, glass, metal, wood, water), body parts (ear, skin, head, heart, hair), clothing, plants, landscapes, and colour, size, texture, temperature, weight and age words (blue, tall, warm, heavy, old) - with its peak on the most concrete noun or physical adjective. It falls to near zero when the same frame carries abstract, social, temporal, numeric or technical content (plan, policy, belief, promise, experience, value, year, code), and it is silent on abstract prose and on code even when those tokens are frequent.

The pole fires on a token that is a fragment inside a numeral-anchored, period-separated non-word string: the single letter of a dotted time abbreviation immediately after a number ('9 a.m.', '5 p.m.', '10:30 a.', '7:45 p.'), the period that follows such a letter, and the digit groups and periods of a dotted address ('192.168.0.1'), reaching 1.0-2.1 (0.5-1.0 of the pole's maximum) there. It collapses to ~0 when the same abbreviation is spelt without periods ('9 am', '7 pm', '10:30 am'), when the same letter has no numeral before it ('the a', 'e.g.', 'i.e.', 'U.S.A.', 'Ph.D.'), on sentence-final periods and across ordinary prose, except for a weaker offshoot on the single-character tag name after '' 1.37, '' 1.48, '

' 0.42, versus '' 0.10).

Fires on prose that is about a piece of authored content and what it contains - a novel, film, album, TV series, comic, game, magazine, article or manual - and on the summarising vocabulary that presents such a work (brief, detailed, comprehensive, summary, overview, explanation, review, illustrated, narrative, genre, synopsis, published, author, format). It stays near zero on prose with no work or document to name or describe: physical objects, machines, science, law and ordinary events, even when the same verbs and adjectives are used.

Retrospectively fires on the token that continues or completes a precise technical, code, or measured-quantity construction — a symbol inside a formula or code expression cued by single-letter variables, parens, operators, digits, or library names (O(n log n), numpy, a + b, = 1, <h1>, print(i), p.m.), or a quantity-plus-unit or fixed collocation (billion light-years, days of heavy rain, converts light energy) — as signaled by the preceding 1-4 tokens; the same surface token (log, heavy, light, +, 1) in plain prose stays near silent.

N2133+ fires on the language of making, supporting or contesting a claim: the epistemic vocabulary in which a text states what is known, argued, assumed, disputed or in doubt (evidence, hypothesis, premise, criteria, valid/invalid, claim, submit, confirm, conclude, dispute, cause, 'not true'), and, in scientific, medical and legal writing, on the specialist term such a claim is made about (autosomal, meningitidis, falciparum, indisputable, aneurysm), with the peak on that word or on the function word introducing it, usually at its first sub-word chunk. It stays at its GELU floor on narrative, dialogue, instructions, plain description, sports reporting and simple promotional copy that make no claim, even when those contain the same learned words used descriptively or evaluatively ('the plot is linear', 'the company's prognosis', 'dedicated counsel', 'she read the diagnosis'); a single learned word or one bare general sentence ('every case is different') is not enough, so the clause needs a run of claim or specialist-assertion language.

This pole fires on tokens that are part of standard open-source license header/disclaimer boilerplate read inside code comments or license strings (e.g. the GPL 'distributed in the hope that it will be useful' warranty disclaimer, the Apache 'you may not use this file except' clause, the MIT 'other dealings' disclaimer, the BSD redistribution clause). The same content words in ordinary non-license prose do not activate it, so it detects the multi-token license-boilerplate context, not individual trigger tokens.

N2296+ fires throughout technical specification prose — passages that describe the construction or operation of an apparatus or a procedure, as in patent specifications, engineering manuals and programming documentation — and peaks on the content words of such passages: part nouns ('shaft', 'bore', 'housing', 'insert') and their reference numerals ('12', '14', '10', '16'). It is near zero on narrative, news, dialogue and promotional prose, and the register dominates the vocabulary (everyday nouns placed in the same patent-style frame fire as strongly as technical ones), though a few nouns that recur in specifications ('surface', 'head', 'body', 'object') also fire weakly in neutral sentences.

This pole fires retrospectively when the current token completes a familiar, semantically coherent multi-token frame: a fixed expression ('at sea level', 'Once upon a'), a selectionally fitting subject-verb or verb-object combination ('telescope captured', 'opened the door'), or a completed clause capped by 'and' or sentence-final '.'. Strength is set by the fit of the preceding ~3 tokens, so the identical peak token goes quiet when an incongruous word is substituted anywhere inside that frame, while edits downstream of the peak have no effect.

The pole fires on the words that carry the meaning 'an indeterminate amount of an unbounded substance or abstraction': (a) quantifier/measure/partitive words used over a bare, unindividuated noun - 'much', 'more', 'less', 'little', 'enough', 'some', 'a lot of', 'lots of', 'plenty of', 'amount(s) of', 'quantity of', 'lack of', 'a pinch/cup/spoonful/pound of', 'how much' - which fire on the quantifier itself whatever noun follows, and stand at 2.0-2.9 against 0.1-0.3 for 'many'/'number of' or for a bare comparative ('much taller' 0.15, 'much better' 0.6); (b) the mass/abstract nouns such amounts apply to when they are introduced indefinitely - 'water', 'food', 'work', 'time', 'money', 'evidence', 'research', 'attention', 'damage', 'rain', 'rice', 'salt', 'coffee' - and an attributive modifier standing directly before such an unbounded head ('hard work' 2.5 vs 'a hard chair' 0.0, 'heavy rain' vs 'a heavy box', 'tap/drinking water', 'media/political attention', 'strong growth' 1.4 vs 'strong results' 0.2); the peak is usually on the quantifying or modifying token one to two tokens before the mass noun (and on the mass noun itself when nothing quantifies it, e.g. 'rice' 0.9 in 'the recipe calls for rice'). It is weak or silent on countable, individuated or already-definite referents and on degree-of-a-property uses of the same words ('the water is cold', 'number of cars', 'some of the boys', 'he bought a red car yesterday'), and a second trigger fires on the first, not-yet-resolved piece of an unfamiliar multi-piece word, usually a substance or technical term ('chives', 'leeks', 'gluten', 'salmonella', 'retinopathy', 'whiplash').

This pole fires when the current token continues a specific overlearned multi-token formula — a memorized collocation, idiom, code or markup idiom, or conventional opening (e.g. 'triangle' in 'follows (directly) from the triangle (inequality)', 'as' in 'import numpy as', 'je' after 'Bonjour,', 'a' in 'Once upon a time, in a', ')' closing 'O(n log n)') — drawing on the preceding ~2-6 tokens. The same token in a non-formulaic frame, or with one frame word replaced, activates weakly or not at all, and strength grows with the canonicity of the full frame rather than with the peak token alone.

Fires on the first sub-word fragment of a rare, technical, foreign or proper-noun word that the tokenizer splits into several pieces, at the point where the fragment cannot plausibly be a complete word in context (e.g. ' Gl'astonbury, ' Ne'umont, ' Lin'q, ' bios'urfactant, ' opens'sh, ' Rod'ríguez, ' an'odization after 'electrochemical'); later fragments of the word get weaker activity, and an inner '.' inside a code identifier/file name before its extension (getQuiz'.'php) also fires. It is near zero on common whole-word tokens, and the same string fires less where it reads as a real word (' an' as an article, ' car' after 'are').

Fires on a word-fragment token that cannot stand as a complete word: most strongly on a bare capital-letter or short onset token (' Z', ' K', ' B', ' Ty', ' Be', ' Ly') that begins an unfamiliar name GPT-2 splits into pieces, often in a name/place slot ('Dr. Z', 'village of K', 'Sargans, Z'), and also on mid-word fragments of rarer words ('r|az|ors') and on tokens inside random alphanumeric strings (URL shortcodes, hashes, passwords). Whole-word tokens (' Smith', ' Oxford', ' Warsaw', ' apples'), ordinary prose and the first token stay near zero, so there is no floor; the response is retrospective, judged from the fragment itself before its continuation is read.

Retrospective detector for the standalone word side (flank/faction/aspect noun): it peaks on the side token itself, boosted by a preceding determiner or locative modifier (the/other/rear), invariant to the following token and to locative versus attributive sense, and exact-token specific (synonym rim and rhymes beside/inside/pride/wide do not substitute). Weaker offshoot peaks on about, left, performance, draw, vention, TH, Fat and Custom are acknowledged secondary responses of the same pole.

Retrospective, essentially context-free detector of a fixed English lexicon of describing and appearing: it fires on the naming/description verbs (called, named, dubbed, termed, described, defined, recognised/recognized, referred, branded, styled), the similarity words (like, such, resembles/resembled/resembling), the appearance words (face, faces, facial, voice, voices, look, looks, looked, expression, complexion, image, picture, shape, profile) and the mental-image verbs (imagined, envisioned, dreamed), more weakly on the quantifiers some, all, any, many and the large numerals million, thousand, hundred, billion, trillion, and on the continuation pieces 'itted', 'anned' and 'akes' (which is why a split 'knitted' or 'scanned' reaches the peak while the same word as a single token, e.g. 'fitted' or 'stakes', does not). It is silent on near-synonyms outside that list (similar, same, comparable, equivalent, appear, seem, form, appearance, figure, visage, label, titled, known, most, more, much, few, several, each, every), on gerund and plural forms (naming, styling, describing, images, pictures, hundreds, thousands, millions), and on concrete count nouns and proper names (cliff, lion, museum, cup, door, table, window, bread, milk, flower, paper, Paris, Japan, Germany), with the copula context ('was/is X') raising every member of the field roughly 0.5-1.0 above its neutral-sentence level.

This pole reads legal-instrument register (legalese), not the topic of law: it is strongly and steadily active across text written in the diction of binding legal documents - statutes, regulations, contracts, leases, terms, tax notices, software-licence disclaimers and court opinions - and near zero on ordinary prose, on journalism about the law, and on plain-English restatements of the same rules. Within such text it peaks on legal-procedural words and the function words embedded in that diction ('motion', 'appeal', 'affirm', 'ineffective', 'provisions', 'pursuant', 'liable'), and a legal-register word earlier in a sentence primes it for later tokens, so the same word ('moved', 'relied') is silent in plain prose.

The pole fires retrospectively on tokens that continue a non-English-prose sequence: mid-word byte-fragments of non-Latin scripts (Cyrillic, Greek, Arabic, CJK/Devanagari byte pieces and replacement-character fragments) and structural delimiters that continue code/data runs (a newline after {/ (, => after ], or a quote closing a digit/comma run). It stays near-inactive on ordinary English prose, including English sentences with Latin-1 mojibake insertions (â/€/™), transliterated foreign words, and quotes or newlines in prose context.
