This negative pole is the GELU trough of a layer-2 neuron's token-level input scalar rather than a detector of its own feature: strength = -gelu_new(pre-activation), so it saturates at the gelu_new global minimum 0.17004 (the scan's max) wherever the pre-activation lies between about -0.5 and -1.5, and it falls back to zero at both ends of that scalar (active only for pre-activations in roughly [-2.03, -0.09]); the neuron's positive lobe is the same scalar seen from the other side, 0.67-0.86 of its 0.868 max on the first token of every prompt and near zero elsewhere. Concretely: predicted inactive (peak below 0.25 x max = 0.0425) for any prompt whose every token is silent - the first token of any sequence, which sits at the scalar's positive end for all 50,257 token types (pre-activation +0.74 to +1.10, so a one-token prompt never fires), light-source/night vocabulary and personal names at the scalar's negative end ('lamp', 'lantern', 'candle', 'glow', 'lights', 'light', 'illumination', 'LED', 'laser', 'brightness', 'night', 'darkness', 'twilight', 'dim', 'moon', 'star', 'Kevin', 'Jason', 'Caroline'), institutional/informational vocabulary and generic quantifiers at its positive end ('policy', 'data', 'information', 'statistics', 'research', 'school', 'business', 'industry', 'email', 'web', 'summary', 'interview', 'history', 'truth', 'should', 'many', 'most', 'enough', 'another'), or the function words 'and', 'of', 'in', 'is', 'for', 'that', 'with', 'as', 'not', 'you', 'my', 'but', 'or', 'at', 'from', 'are', 'an', 'be', 'it', 'was', 'a', ',', '.', newline and '('; predicted active (usually 0.6-1.0 of max, 0.3-0.5 for weaker mid-band words such as ' cat', ' city', ' letter') for any prompt of two or more tokens that contains, from its second position on, an ordinary concrete noun or verb from the middle of the scalar (' table', ' museum', ' committee', ' dog', ' doctor', ' mountain', ' walked', ' approved', ' met'), a colour, a soft-abstract noun ('theory', 'concept', 'idea', 'beauty', 'freedom'), a subword continuation, the articles ' the'/' The', or ' can'/' he'/' has' - so a sentence like 'the lamp was bright' fires on ' was' even though every light word in it is silent.

Largely a lexical detector for a short list of specific tokens, firing on the token itself (active, >0.25 of max): the 'ous' piece of French 'vous'/'nous' (split as ' v'+'ous', 'n'+'ous'), unspaced file-extension 'jar' (in '.jar', but not the English word ' jar'), ' Promise', 'const', ' var', identifier-final 'Array', ' chief', ' district', ' recently', capitalised ' Association', ' reaction' and ' council'. It fires most strongly (near max) when the token is the head of a name-like compound with a preceding modifier ('BJP chief', 'Faizabad district', 'pour vous', 'return Promise', 'app.jar', 'menuArray'), weaker on the bare word ('The chief' ~0.25 of max), and near silent on near-synonyms in the same slot ('leader', 'officer', 'city', 'also', 'zip', 'Object', 'lui').

The pole is a retrospective, form-specific English word-form detector for the seeing/looking family: it peaks on the trigger token itself (79-94% of each peak's integrated-gradients attribution lies on that token, and every occurrence of ' see' (56), ' View' (15) and ' close' (16) in the audit scan is active), firing on the gaze and inspection verbs (see/sees/saw/seen/seeing, view(s)/viewed/viewing/viewer/preview, look(s)/looked/looking/lookout/lookalike, watch(es)/watched/watching/watchful, inspect/inspection(s)/inspected/inspecting/inspector(s), examine/examines/examined/examining/examination(s), check(s)/checked/checking/checker/checkbox, browse/browsed/browsing, scan(s)/scanned/scanning, search/searches/searched/searching, monitor(s)/monitoring, glance(s)/glanced, glimpse(s)/glimpsed, peek(ed/s)/peeking, gaze/gazed, squint(ed/s)/squinting, visit(s)/visited/visiting/visitor(s), tour(s)/toured/touring/tourist(s), sightsee/sightseeing/sighted, lookout, spectator(s)), on the eye and sight nouns (eye(s)/eyed/eyeing/eyeball(s)/eyelid(s)/eyelash(es)/eyebrow(s)/brow(s)/eyesight/sight(s)/visual/visually/visible/visibility/vision/visor/ocular/cornea/retina), and on open(s)/opened/opening/close(s)/closed/closing/closely (weaker, often sub-threshold, on window(s)/tab(s)/preview/browser/scroll and on stare/observe). It is form- rather than sense-driven ('The shop is close to the station' fires as strongly as 'close the browser'), stays near baseline on differently spelled near-synonyms (notice, spot, read, peep, peer, ogle, leer, blink, wink, survey, peruse), on the other senses (hear, listen, smell, taste, touch), on visual-content or gear nouns (image, picture, photo, camera, lens, glasses, video), on web-page nouns (http/www/link/website/page/click/menu) and on aperture words (shut, lock, door, screen, curtain, blind), and its output direction promotes eye/sight vocabulary (Jacobian lens: eye, eyes, gaze, ocular, magnification), so it is retrospective rather than lookahead (zero-ablation leaves next-token predictions almost unchanged: KL 0.003 with no concentrated target set).

Retrospective bigram-chunk completion detector: the pole peaks when the current token is the highly predictable continuation of the immediately preceding token, whether a subword prefix (CO->2, Cont->rast, Spect->ra) or a collocational partner (Earth->orbit, distance->between, of->thrust, miles->below, Over->time); the same token after an unrelated predecessor fires weakly or not at all.

Fires retrospectively on language of a cohesive human collective: nouns for members or bodies of a group (voters, constituents, caucus, committees, members, supporters, friend or foe) and positively-valenced words for the regard, virtue, or act that binds or honors the group (pride, respect, loyalty, devotion, unity, sacred, truly, confer, commit, serve); matched hostile or asocial evaluative words (hatred, scorn, guilt, envy, corrupt) and nonsocial concrete nouns leave it near baseline, and same-suffix or near-homograph controls (prefers, infers, scared) do not substitute.

Fires on the head noun of a noun phrase that names a gradable quantity, dimension or type as a variable being measured, compared or changed (proportion, percentage, number, degree, extent, amount, size, rate, bounds/limits, and kind/sort/type in 'some/the kind of'), strongest right after a determiner plus a verb or adjective of change or magnitude ('decreased the proportion', 'varying number', 'highest percentage', 'upper bounds', 'true extent'), and also on unit tokens like '%' and 'deg'. It stays silent when the same word has a non-quantity sense (a phone number to call or write, an academic degree, 'out of bounds', the verb 'sort') or is a fixed quantifier ('a number of', 'a large number of'), and it is weaker at the start of a sentence ('The number is seven').

Fires retrospectively when the current token completes a conventional two-token chunk begun on the immediately preceding token: a phrasal-verb particle (verb + out/up), a fixed phrase (the same + time/week, called + for), or the second subword of a common word (sle+ek, Swe+at, New+er). Both the preceding trigger and the completing token are required; the same peak token without its trigger is weak.

Fires retrospectively when the current token is a restrictive post-nominal specifier that narrows the head noun in the immediately preceding 1-2 tokens, such as an adjective/adverb (far in kingdom far), a clause keyword (WHERE after users), a past participle (stored in energy stored), or a number (13 in galaxy 13). It stays near zero on sentence-initial tokens and on prenominal or non-restricting continuations even when the same content words appear.

This pole fires on the token that completes a highly predictable local multi-token unit: the particle, preposition, ordinal, or word-piece that finishes a stock collocation fixed by the preceding word or words (e.g. broke+down, listen/prior+to, ran+into, kick/spin+off, break+up, season+one/airing, print+out, built+in, precomp+iled, OP+IN). Activation is graded by how strongly the left context constrains the token rather than by the token's identity, so the same surface token fires weakly or not at all in less constraining contexts (calmed/came+down, speak+to, season+five).

This pole is a retrospective detector for social-institutional and technical content morphemes: dress and presentation words (dressed, wearing, suit, linen), work-economics nouns (labor, capital), and bound pieces of code identifiers and technical names (iss in isset, und in undef, en language/name codes, red/nex/vers/aked fragments), firing when such a token itself is read. It stays near zero on function words, on bleached high-frequency general nouns and verbs (ready, work, money, bag, holding, rules, clean), and on concrete physical-object nouns (dog, house, car, table, steel), and Jacobian-promoted words like textile do not drive it, so it reports a recognized input rather than preparing an upcoming token.

Fires retrospectively when the current token names or completes a physically co-present group of people (crowd, audience) or the concrete venue, room, vehicle, vessel, or landscape that situates them (stage, office, warehouse, room, SUV, limousine, beach, shore), or describes characters' bodily movement, placement, or audible collective action relative to that setting (walk, arrives, headed, around, outside, wave); it does not fire on abstract, institutional, or technical uses of similar strings.

Retrospective detector for continuation seams inside an ongoing enumerative or parallel structure (bulleted/numbered/plain lists, table rows and column gaps, repeated code-block lines, runs of parallel items): it fires on the gap whitespace — line breaks, indent runs, inter-column spaces — at second-or-later item boundaries, and on light sentence-initial continuation words (pronouns such as they/them, conjuncts such as yet) that resume discourse after such a structure. It stays near zero on plain-prose paragraph breaks, ordinary single inter-word spaces, and first-item boundaries, and requires on the order of 20–40 preceding tokens of the enumerative structure.

Fires retrospectively on words denoting an institutionally or socially assigned standing of a person, object, or quantity: prior or founding role (former, founder, owner), rank (first), quantity (number), exchange value (cost, price), change of state or possession (conversion, transfer), or asserted entitlement (claiming, owning). It peaks on the whole token for single-token words and on the non-initial piece for BPE-split words (K+ering, back+ped+aled, re+interpret); strength grades down to related words (value, worth, delivery, latter, last) and to ~0 on concrete near-neighbors (prize, bill, farmer, lumber, load, count, most). It does not prepare any specific upcoming token: the Jacobian-lens promoted list is incoherent with kurtosis ~3.1 and the tokens after peaks vary freely (MI6 chief, of, code, associated, $7, -rate, proposed).

Fires retrospectively on a word that denotes a unit of informational or cognitive content, i.e. something that can be said, known, thought about or asked about (idea, answer, result, advice, problem, question, point, example, reason, conclusion, explanation, comment, message, reply, story, warning, outcome, fact, thing, way, detail, feature, opinion, view), and on the demonstrative and anaphoric third-person pronouns that stand in for such content (this, these, it, that, those, they, them). Concrete objects (table, lamp, bottle, ladder, window), persons (man, friend, doctor), places, body parts, human pronouns (him, her, me, you), universal pronouns (everything, nothing, everyone), and abstract nouns that carry no propositional content (justice, love, anger, money, law, music, health, knowledge, understanding, value, case, effect) predict low activity.

Fires on the current token when it opens a new constituent: a preposition beginning a PP or time/place adjunct (at, in, on, by, of), a copula or auxiliary beginning a predicate (are, is), a clause linker (then, so, in), a VP-initial verb (stared, scored, stepped, fell), or a word- or clause-initial keyword or subword that starts a new lexical, code, or markup item (Se, zer, prot, h, ORDER, O, powerhouse, je, a); the peak is on the onset token itself, not the preceding boundary.

L4/N123+ fires retrospectively on the token that opens the predicate or body of a construction once its preamble has closed: in prose the finite verb, auxiliary or complementizer that directly follows a full lexical subject noun phrase ('the report shows', 'the cave was', 'the survey found', 'the era began', 'found that'), and the comma, question mark or line break that ends a fronted clause, salutation, signature or question together with the first word of the clause that follows ('...fonts, open a terminal', '...tools, all options are grayed out', '...challenges?<nl><nl>This article...'), with the analogous code block opener '{', '///' or 'import' after a signature or line start. It falls below the active threshold where the same token merely continues the phrase it is already inside - the same verb after a pronoun, adverb or modal ('it shows' 0.34, 'strongly shows' 0.35, 'will show' 0.36 against 'the report shows' 0.88), a preposition after the head noun ('the report of' 0.00), a relativiser after a noun ('the plan that' 0.05) - while the peak grows with the completeness of the preamble ('the report of the plan shows' 1.24 > 'the report shows' 0.88).

The pole fires on a content word that is the head of a phrase rather than a modifier of one: the main verb of a declarative clause, or the participle, predicate adjective or post-modal adverb (ever, never, always) that carries its verb phrase, once the clause's subject or a modal/auxiliary has been read; and the head noun of a possessive or noun-noun phrase ('its weight', "the article's", 'body weight'). It stays near zero on the same words when they are used attributively before another noun ('the available results', 'a falling document', 'capacity building', 'weight loss').

L4/N159+ fires on the token that closes a fused two-token unit, i.e. the second member of a chunk that names a single lexical item: a hyphen or prefix/particle compound (in-house, after-school, out-of-date, over|harvesting, run|ny, Port|ales) or a fixed preposition/particle-headed expression (in place, in mind, into play, into force, cut short, top out, at bay, end of). Both members are required (replacing the earlier token erases essentially the whole activation, and that earlier token never fires alone), while the same words as free compositional constituents (a place, take place, your mind, in order, in line, in which, of the, in house, farmhouse, on site) and the token after the completed unit stay at baseline; the output side carries no coherent next-token set (Jacobian kurtosis 3.06, 0% agreement with the logit lens), so this is retrospective chunk-detection, not lookahead.

Retrospective detector for the information-bearing, distinctive piece of a conventionalized multiword unit: the word-initial (or standalone) Latinate/Greek technical morpheme (aux-, syn-, ex-, hypothal-, synchron-, dorsal, -os-), a locative particle (inside, within, through), the @ of an XML resource reference, or an emphatic copular pronoun (It is us). It fires on that token given its disambiguating left context (background=", sensitivity to, being, it is) and stays near zero on matched common, fused, or compositional counterparts (exotic, chronic, normal, mutant, among us, email @).

In written expository prose this pole fires on the word that names the property, structure or category being characterised - usually the head of a definite noun phrase such as 'the composition of the mixture', 'the structure of the protein', 'the layout of the building', 'the ratio/colour/symmetry/condition of X' (composition, structure, layout, ratio, distribution, symmetry, colour, density, condition, mutation, toxin, hydrogen, protein) - and on the connective of a frame that introduces such a term ('As for X' / 'As to X', 'the definition of X', 'a model for X'), and on code declaration keywords (class, import, namespace). It stays near zero on narrative and conversational text and on everyday concrete or event nouns in the same slots (dog, lunch, owner, purpose, kettle, party, sandwich, feedback).

This pole fires on graphic, non-prose tokens rather than on ordinary lowercase words: numerals, quotation marks and initials closed by a period, with the sharpest peak on the period that closes the numeral abbreviation 'No.'/'Nos.' (mean 1.84 across the scan's 24 such tokens, all >= 0.5, up to the 2.33 maximum). Its response to numerals and to quoted terms is strongly amplified when that marked token is the head of a determiner phrase ('a 3-D', 'the 40HX803', 'the "license"', 'a 3' = 1.2-1.3 vs 0.0-0.2 with no determiner), while plain lowercase words - especially the most frequent function words ('of', 'and', 'in', 'for') - leave it at zero.

GPT-2 L4/N420 is an abstract-relation detector: its positive pole fires on abstract/relational nouns and nominalizations ('construction', 'reduction', 'importance', 'nature', 'outcome', 'role', 'relationship') and then across the complement phrase such a head governs ('of/between' + 'the' + complement noun, e.g. 'reduction of the cost' = +0.95, +1.55, +0.71, +0.92), while staying off on the matching verb/adjective ('constructed', 'reduced', 'important', 'related') and on physical or concrete heads ('building', 'length', 'width', 'position', 'battle', 'cat'); its input row's top vocabulary projections are the nominalizing suffixes 'eness', 'itiveness', 'itivity', 'fulness', 'ation', 'ology', 'fficiency'. The negative pole is that same unit switched off: its strength is the depth of the GELU pre-activation below zero, so it saturates at GELU's floor (0.17004, which is why 18 of 20 scan peaks are 0.169-0.170 and the whole scan's maximum is that floor) on every token that is not inside such a phrase - predict it ACTIVE (peak >= 0.0425 of scale) for any prompt containing ordinary concrete, verbal or connective prose, and expect it to fall toward the activity line only for short prompts whose tokens all continue an abstract nominalization phrase ('The reduction of the cost was welcomed' peaks at 0.072 against 0.161 for 'The painting of the cost was welcomed').

Fires retrospectively on the token that completes a conventional verb/preposition + complement collocation stating the outcome, manner-of-success, or resultant state of an action (e.g. works fine/well, tested positive, in contact, into focus/effect, came to fruition, be displayed) — i.e. when the current token is the predictable second half of a frequent outcome/state bigram, requiring both halves, so replacing either half with a non-collocate collapses activation.

This pole is retrospective: it peaks on the token that completes a state, position, or time predicate's argument frame -- the object determiner after 'opened', the locative 'on' after posture verbs (sat/sits/stood/lay), the participle in a 'Where are you going' question, or a day/time noun continuing an opening-hours expression ('opens Tuesday', 'Tuesday morning') -- and stays at floor on the same tokens outside those frames ('the' after closed/ate/saw, 'on' after slept/fell, 'going' in declaratives, 'Tuesday' after every/you). The Jacobian lens is incoherent (kurtosis 3.1) and integrated-gradients attribution sits on the 1-3 preceding tokens, so it reacts to the predicate already read rather than preparing an upcoming token.

Fires retrospectively when the current token names or describes the natural environment or the cultivation of land: forests, grasslands, wetlands, wildlife habitat, farm and forestry life, and ecological adjectives such as natural, environmental, and sustainable, generalizing to class members absent from the scan peaks (savanna, meadow, wetland). It also has a secondary token-level sensitivity to the 'CO' subtoken in carbon/Colorado uses (CO2, 2016 COA citations) that drives it even without ecological content.

This pole fires on the word that fulfills a frequent circumstantial or naming frame: a spatial/temporal linker (around, at, before) completing a copular, existential, or negative clause frame ('was/been around', 'was at', 'nothing at all', 'never seen that before'), or the complement completing a fixed adverbial or naming formula ('at night', 'at all', 'as its name suggests'). Activation is graded by frame familiarity, so the same linker in an uncommon frame ('happened around', 'its title states') or replaced by a non-linker fires weakly; subword fragments (dell, Haupt) and headings (Background) are leftovers.

This pole is the GELU-off side of N299: it sits at a ~0.10-0.17 baseline on ordinary non-initial tokens and shuts off to ~0 on the sequence-first token and on the function-word positions where the positive pole fires (infinitival/prepositional 'to', 'into', demonstratives like 'this', possessives like 'your'). It depends only on the current and immediately preceding tokens (mean IG distance ~2 tokens), so it is retrospective, not a next-token predictor (Jacobian kurtosis ~3.1, incoherent promoted list).

The pole fires on the token that spells out a personal name - a given name (' Sarah', ' David', ' Pete'), a surname (' Wilson', ' Fernandez'), or an interior BPE fragment or initial of one ('airo' inside ' Nairobi', 'ian' in ' Maximilian', a byline ' H') - and the peak is set jointly by the token's name-likeness and by whether the preceding words make a person the expected referent (after 'by', 'and', 'said', 'named' or a title such as 'Dr'/'author' real names reach 1.4-2.5; in a neutral sentence the same name reaches only 0.4-0.9). It reads exactly 0.00 on organisation/brand names ('Microsoft', 'Google', 'IBM', 'NATO', 'Harvard') in every plain frame and only about 0.9 when a title forces a person reading ('Dr Microsoft'), 0.00 on lowercase common nouns and on place names in place frames ('The capital of France is Paris/Madrid'), about 0.2 when a determiner immediately precedes the name ('the Sarah'), and 0.00 on every token of a name that opens the text ('Sarah arrived at the office early').

L5/N428+ is a sentence-onset lexical detector: it fires on the first word of a new sentence - the content word that begins immediately after a sentence boundary (a period, question mark, or a paragraph/line break), with the peak usually inside that first word's sub-tokens (e.g. ' Resorption', ' Gait', ' Practitioners', ' Milk'). It is near zero on the boundary punctuation itself, on the same content word when it sits mid-sentence or after a comma, and on sentences that open with a pronoun, determiner or discourse connective (' It', ' The', ' However'); across the scan, sentence-onset content words average 0.57 with 25% above 1.0, versus 0.18 for sentence-onset function words and -0.08 for every other token.

Retrospective detector for a stake - an amount of good or ill that accrues to a party: it is active (0.25-0.8 of the 2.18 scan maximum) on the content word that names the stake (harm, damage, injury, risk, threat, danger, cost, fee, debt, toll, burden / benefit, advantage, gain, profit, reward, success, value, protection / chance, likelihood / rise, drop, increase, decline, reduction) and on the attitude words that presuppose one (grateful, proud, pleased, afraid, hopeful, thrilled, shame, pride), and it stays active across the rest of the stake phrase, so the connective that assigns the stake to its holder or condition, and the possessive naming that holder, are often its peak ('a clear benefit [[for]] the patients' 1.43, 'the risk [[of]] failure' 0.95, 'She was fired [[from]] [[her]] job' 2.10/1.12, 'it would help me [[if]] I had it' 2.31). It stays at the GELU floor (0.00-0.15) on words that name a situation rather than an amount of welfare (problem, crisis, disaster, accident, emergency, issue, setback - all exactly 0.00 in frames where the matching stake word scores 0.7-1.7), on accounting nouns (money, tax, loan, insurance, and literal 'value' in code), on diffuse negative emotion (angry, worried, sad, disappointed, satisfied, guilty), on neutral abstracts (idea, plan, question, result, outcome, level, amount) and on concrete nouns, so the same slot 'The X to the company was enormous' fires on damage/benefit/cost/risk and is 0.00 on letter/reply/problem, while 'value' fires as a verb ('we truly value your support', 0.67) but not as a variable name (0.10); 'loss' and 'penalty' are an unexplained boundary case (0.0-0.25 in most frames, 0.58 once) and two leftovers are not covered by the main claim: a few rare subword pieces fire whatever the word means ('url' inside Wurlitzer 1.42-1.60 but 'url' alone 0.00, 'ns' inside hens 1.21), and 'calcium' fires (0.77) where vitamin, protein, cholesterol and other dietary words stay at 0.00.

Fires retrospectively when the current token completes a clause-level discourse-organizing connective or focusing adverbial — of course, for instance, first/firstly/secondly/finally/first off plus comma, especially/particularly, as well (as), on top of that, also/there is also the — that frames the clause as elaboration, enumeration, or emphasis. It does not fire on the same content words in literal non-discourse roles or when the fixed connective frame is broken.

The pole fires on the clause's relational vocabulary rather than on words that name or point at an entity: it peaks on subordinating/wh-words and the degree adverbs they take (when, if, while, until, where, how + well/easily/far), on circumstance prepositions (under, at, from, during, across, within, through, beyond) and on modals/auxiliaries plus the verb or adjective they govern (should, must, do/does/did, need). It stays near zero on nouns, determiners (a, the), numerals, coordinating conjunctions (and, or), accusative pronouns (them, him) and on purely grammatical prepositions/relatives (by, with, of, for, that, which), even when those words are equally frequent in context.

Fires on the token that completes a unit strongly constrained by earlier tokens at any grain: the subword finishing a word (airo, umpy), the preposition, verb, or adjective filling the slot a verb or noun opened (fell to, rushed into, function returns, days of heavy rain), or the keyword closing a code or markup frame (FROM, </body>). Strength scales with how tightly the opener constrains the completion, so swapping the opener for one that does not select the same continuation collapses activity on the identical token.

The pole fires when text attributes a restricted or alternative identity to something: minimizers before a predicate noun ('just/simply/merely/only a X', 'a mere X', 'nothing/little/no more than a X', 'essentially/basically a X'), limiting adverbs of proportion ('primarily/mainly/mostly/partly of'), contrastive-alternative pivots ('not X but Y', 'X rather than Y', 'instead of', 'as opposed to', 'versus', 'prefer X to Y'), and more weakly source/composition/scope predications ('originated from', 'composed of', 'based on', 'confined to'). The peak sits on the pivot token itself -- the 'than', 'but' or 'versus', the 'of'/'to' of the substitute phrase, or the determiner opening the downgraded noun phrase -- and the pole stays near zero when the same words lack that function: temporal 'just now', quantifier 'only a few', additive 'simply put', plain contrast 'small but clean', numeric 'more than fifty', plain copula 'is a X', or set exclusion 'except/apart from'.

N2076+ is a retrospective detector for a substantive, open-class English word: it fires on the token that carries a concrete, specific or lower-frequency noun, adjective, participle or adverb (flood, source, weight, seed, oxygen, hunger, previously, elected, retrieved), and stays near zero on high-frequency function words and punctuation (the, and, of, with, than, ?, :). Its single strongest input is the rare byte token 'âĢ' that begins a curly apostrophe or quote in English (’s, ’re, ’ll) — the straight ASCII apostrophe triggers nothing — and within a given word it fires hardest where the left context sharply constrains the next token.

The pole fires on content words that name a designated role, part or relational attribute of a larger structured whole: role nouns for a position held inside an organisation (client, director, guard, resident, intern, assistant, architect, author), part/region words for a body or structure (head, arm, eye, ear, leg, foot, neck, chest, joint, limb, posterior, anterior, ventral, dermal, arterial, cranial), and the derived attributive form of a relational verb that describes an entity by what it is tied to (X-based, X-related, X-associated, X-dependent, X-protected, X-reserved, X-controlled, X-governed, functional, conditional). It fires on that word itself wherever it appears after the first token of the text, and stays at its floor on the everyday core vocabulary even inside the same categories (customer, hand, knee, heart, skin, bone), on generic category and technical nouns (element, section, component, department, protein, algorithm, variable) and on bare formal/legal words (herein, aforementioned).

The pole fires at the point where a general, characterizing claim - what something is, or is generally like, rather than a report of a one-off event - is grounded or defined, peaking on the connector that carries the relation: 'since', 'as' or 'because' introducing its reason or evidence ('Plants need water since they cannot store it'; 'as' also fires in 'as well as' and evidential 'as shown by'), 'refers to' in a definition, and, more weakly, the period that ends such a claim. It stays inactive when the same words mark time, comparison, exemplification, concession or consequence ('since 2010', 'as big as', 'such as', 'although', 'so'), and when a because/since clause explains a one-off event ('The window shattered because the ball hit it').

Peaks on the discourse pointer see/See (including the please-see frame), plus the sibling redirect openers please/Please before a navigation verb and here in hereafter, when the token functions as an imperative cross-reference redirecting the reader to content located elsewhere (another section, document, page, or a term defined below); it stays quiet on perceptual or cognitive uses of see such as I see what you mean and when the pointer is replaced by a non-redirect word.

L6/N489+ is a register-and-domain detector for characterising prose about people, culture and institutions. It is active throughout encyclopedic/biographical, news and arts-or-business writing, where it peaks on the ordinary carrier words of those sentences - above all the indefinite article ' a'/' an', ' has', ' in', ' into', ' from', ' the', ' of', ' to', ' with', ' as', and the '.'/'\n' that closes a sentence or section - and on light content words of that field (' law', ' art', ' music', ' poetry', ' novel', ' film', ' career', ' teacher', ' compliance', ' appeared'); the same words carry no activation when they sit in episodic action narrative ('she walked into the room'), in physical/technical or object description ('the chemical engineer calibrated the spectrometer'), in mathematics or in code, which sit at baseline (~0.00 mean, versus ~0.18-0.24 mean in biography documents).

The pole fires on a noun phrase that 'of' binds to a complement it belongs to: the noun-internal 'of' itself, the head noun just before it, and the determiner that follows it ('the head of the department' 0.6/1.2/1.0, 'those of earlier studies' 1.5), and it stays at the floor where 'of' instead completes a verb or a fixed idiom ('accused them of theft', 'consists of water', 'died of cancer', 'approved of the plan'). The same 'of' is much weaker when the phrase is introduced by a possessive or indefinite determiner rather than 'the' ('our head of ...' about zero, 'a head of ...' about half of 'the head of ...'), and its strength is graded by how tightly the head noun names a part or attribute of the complement ('head/top/back/beginning of' 0.6-1.2 versus 'author/colour/name of' 0.1-0.4).

This pole fires at the seam between two discourse units: its strongest trigger is the newline that ends a syntactically complete line of structured text (a completed clause, a colon-introduced list, or an HTML/code line), and in running prose it fires on the function word that opens the next clause or noun phrase instead of continuing the current one ('since', 'because', 'whenever', 'each', 'every', 'only', 'more', 'less', 'right'). A newline that splits a phrase fires at about half strength and coordinators ('and', 'but', 'or'), commas, semicolons and periods do not fire, so the peak is a retrospective read of the unit just completed rather than preparation of a specific next token (Jacobian-lens kurtosis 3.2, promoted-token list incoherent).

The pole fires on the word that introduces negative polarity into a clause: the negators no, not, n't, never, nobody, nothing, none, neither, nor, without, cannot, plus the negative quantifiers/downtoners few, little, hardly, barely, scarcely, seldom, rarely, zero, lack and the negating predicates unable, impossible, unlikely, denied, refused. Its output direction writes that negative-polarity signal forward and promotes exactly the negative-polarity items such a clause licenses ('any', 'anything', 'anyone', 'anybody', 'anywhere', 'ever', 'anymore', 'slightest', 'nor'); it stays at baseline on the positive counterparts of the same strings (a few, a little, some, all, many, always, with), on negative-sounding words that do not negate (false, incorrect, unclear, inaccurate, stopped, forgot, only, at most, less than), and on the same letters inside longer words (notable, note, north, Nottingham).

This pole fires on a word that states a person's professional role, employment action, or credential — titles like assistant/associate, employment verbs like serves, worked, work, plays, taught, or apply — when it occurs inside a third-person biographical or organizational description, with the person's background before it and an affiliation complement (as, at, for, to, or a role noun like director or Attorney) after it. The same word outside such a person-description frame, or a non-role word in the same slot, activates it weakly or not at all.

A tonic (default-on) pole: it sits near its 0.17 ceiling on most non-initial tokens (nouns, adjectives like ' old'/' new', determiners ' the', object pronouns, infinitival ' to', word pieces, numbers, punctuation), i.e. wherever the pre-activation is mildly negative (about -0.4 to -1.3). It is silent at the first position and on the neuron's positive-pole tokens, which are copulas/auxiliaries right after a subject (' is', ' are', ' am') and stative/locative relation words (' lives', ' in', ' on', ' at', ' by' after 'is'/'live'). It is also weak (<0.06) where the pre-activation is driven strongly negative, mainly on nationality or ethnic adjectives (' American', ' German', ' Chinese', ' Jewish') and '+' operators, and somewhat lower on possessives ' his'/' its'.

The pole fires at the point where a text commits to a specific amount, measure or target: on numerals and on the punctuation, scale words and unit nouns inside quantity expressions (decimal points, thousands groups, 'million'/'thousand'/'hundred', 'percent', 'metres'/'feet'/'years'), on the bracket that opens a metric equivalent or gloss after a term ('8 inches (200 mm)', 'Minoxidil (Rogaine)'), on months inside dates, and on the 'to'/'in' that introduces the target or time of an orientation, response or suitability predicate (appeal/cater/speak/attend/respond/adapt + to, due in, intended/tailor-made for). It stays quiet on vague quantifiers (many, several, very), on plain counts inside a narrative frame ('there were 30 people in the room', 'the meeting lasted 30 minutes'), and on reference or motion 'to' ('refer to the rules', 'walked to the store').

This pole fires when the just-read token is a one- or two-character word-initial fragment that still needs its tail to finish a split Romance-language or proper-name word (e.g. ' t' starting tous/tanto/tengo, ' T' starting TOWN/Tastiest, 't' inside politica, 'y' inside Diyas, 'it' inside Fioritura), or a closed-set determiner or size adjective in attributive position before its noun (' the', ' el'/' del', ' tu', ' little'/' small'/' tiny'/' enormous'/' Grand' — e.g. of the Congo, the little boy, Giro del Sestriere, Grand Hotel); the hottest pieces (' t', ' el', ' tu') also fire standalone or metalinguistically. It stays inactive on other determiners and non-size adjectives (' every', ' a', ' stray', ' pinch'), on the same gated tokens in complete, final, or predicative use (' Model T', 'found it', 'x y z', 'seems little'), and on fragments of long ordinary English words such as antidisestablishmentarianism or counterrevolutionary.

Fires retrospectively when the current token is a masculine third-person pronoun (he/He/his/His) referring to a male person in the surrounding discourse, or the final subtoken of a male proper name or male-associated title. The same leading-space ' he' surface form also triggers word-internally (e.g. heirloom -> he + irloom) as a token-shape false positive.

Fires on a word-initial BPE fragment that is not itself a word and must be completed by the next token(s), typically with no leading space after punctuation, a quote, a slash or a newline: 'qu'(iz/arie), 'gu'(ides/idance), 'per'(mission), 'reg'(ulations), 'requ'(ests), 'P'(ete), 'Q'(A), 'Rep'(onses). It also fires more weakly (about 0.4-0.85 of max) on political or office-title words before a name or role, such as ' Sen', ' Rep', ' Policy', ' Senior', ' Democratic', ' Republican' and ' Party'. Ordinary whole-word tokens and plain prose stay near 0, and the first token of any prompt is always ~0 (so 'Sen. X' or 'quiz' at position 0 does not fire).

The pole fires on discourse-anaphoric and scope-marking expressions whose content is fixed by earlier discourse: prototypically 'so' retrieving a prior proposition, list, or name (said/think so, and so on/forth, so-called, so far, even so), plus functional relatives in the same role (to the extent/degree, except, as, such). It stays near floor when the same tokens are used non-anaphorically, especially degree-intensifier 'so' (was/felt so + gradable adjective), approximator 'or so', or unrelated content words (very, etc., creams, offers). The same onset-matching extends to memorized routine continuations where the peak lands on a word-initial fragment (the 'so' of 'soaps', the 'g' of 'which gives' after a line break, surname-initial 'G' after a newline or handle boundary), which drive it while same-frame non-routine substitutions do not.

This pole fires retrospectively when the current token is a coherent phrase-internal continuation of the immediately preceding 1-2 tokens, completing an abbreviation (a.m.), markup tag (h1), word-piece (N-airo), verb argument (raised interest), reporting-verb complement (announced she), determiner phrase (submit your, the triangle), prepositional complement (of fraud), list item (name, email), or subject-verb / coordination chunk (recipe calls, pan and). It stays low when the identical token starts a new clause, follows a clause boundary or selectionally incoherent context (painted she, recipe sleeps, door and [clause]), or is replaced by an unfitting token. Changing only post-peak tokens leaves the peak unchanged.

The pole is a retrospective detector for procedural or instructional text: it is active in source code, in step-by-step instructions (how-tos, UI navigation, recipes) and in manual or specification sentences that say what to do or what a system does, and it is near-silent (below 0.1 x max) in prose that narrates people and events - fiction, news, and legal or contract writing; the same content roughly doubles when it is phrased as an imperative rather than a third-person declarative. Within an active passage it peaks on the operative token - the step's verb ('Click', 'go', 'save'), an operator or the dot of a qualified name ('=', '->', '+=', '.' in 'forms.py'), a code keyword ('include', 'import', 'from', 'if', 'WHERE', 'package'), or the connective that opens the next step ('Then', 'then', 'and') - so a single token moves more than twenty-fold with context: ' Then' is 0.34 in a story and 2.94 in an instruction.

Fires retrospectively on the current token when its spelling belongs to a narrow orthographic class: go/do-verb forms (going/went/go/goes/do/did/done), made/see/rode/lone-type forms, short capitalized word-fragments (Cou, Lou, Made, Pro, Analy, fue, Go, DO, PI, Se, ode), vowel letters (A/O/U/Y/E, o/u) and the digit 4 — with homophone pairs split purely by spelling (see>sea, made>maid, rode>road, do>due, lone>loan) — while staying silent on consonant letters, other digits, complete common proper nouns (Ann, Cairo, Paris), th-words, regular verbs (walking, left, showed) and take/know/eat/say paradigms; left context gates strength (date/list contexts boost fragments; fixed constructions like 'Vitamin E', 'Flight 4', pronominal 'I' and perfect-tense 'seen' veto it). It does not prepare any specific upcoming token: the Jacobian lens is near-Gaussian (kurtosis 3.4) and its promoted g-fragments never follow the peaks.

Fires on the introducer slot of a conventional frame that presents an act or stance of directed regard, attention, or evaluation — e.g. keep in __, keep/turned a __, caught/brought to my __, (have) expressed/drew __, came under __, took/receiving particular __, (it) is with __, also of __ — peaking on the frame's verb, preposition, possessive, or evaluative adjective. Swapping the complement noun (eye/ball, interest/anger, scrutiny/repair, attention/water) leaves the peak unchanged while swapping the introducing verb (caught->saw, expressed->stated, brought->walked, keep->walk) collapses it, so the trigger is the frame already read, not the upcoming word.

N2697+ is a retrospective detector for closed-class wording that carries extent or quantity in generic, habitual or directive English, not for those words as such: it peaks on both 'as' tokens of an 'as ... as' comparative of extent ('as quickly as possible', 'as much as you can', 'as soon as possible') whatever word fills the middle or follows, on 'every' in a habitual sentence ('We eat out every Friday'), and on the indefinite article or quantifier in an imperative or light-verb frame ('Take a few seconds', 'Please take a ...'). It stays silent on bare prepositional 'as' ('as a rule', 'as the manager asked', 'as the author of this work'), on the definite article in the same slot ('Take the photo'), and on the same closed-class words inside specific third-person narration ('He took a seat', 'I saw a photo').

The pole fires at the licensing head of a clause that predicates a state, condition, capacity, property, or category membership of an entity: on copular/linking verbs (be, become, remain, seem) after a typically animate subject, on the object pronoun of causative small clauses (make/find/keep it ADJ), on predicate-internal negators and degree words, and on linkers or punctuation right after such a predication completes. Its output direction promotes the upcoming predicative state/capability adjectives (liable, prone, susceptible, vulnerable, eligible, responsible). It does not fire on lexical verbs or referential objects occupying the same slots.

This pole fires retrospectively on the content word that completes a noun phrase fixing which group, how many, or which party is meant: a number or quantifier after frames like 'No.', 'for', 'additional', or 'OF' (55, 7, 11, 4, 12, four, ANY, number), or a plural/abstract group-denoting head noun after 'the'/'a'/an adjective (plaintiffs, Department, treatments, viewers, you), including the comma that closes such a group appositive. It does not fire on the preceding function words alone, nor when the same slot holds an adjective, article, adverb, or unrelated concrete noun.

Retrospective detector for a mid-clause determiner or preposition (a/the/in/to/on/at) that opens or continues a post-verbal object, locative/goal/temporal adjunct, or enumerated noun phrase (e.g. 'into the hallway', 'in a kingdom', 'to the pan', 'and a pinch', 'from 9 a.m.'). Strength is graded by governor and context: maximal after a rich descriptive clause with a placement/transfer/motion verb, moderate in short clauses, weak in fixed collocations ('times a day', 'on the mat'), copular/light-verb frames ('carry a negative', 'sits on'), and zero on sentence-initial determiners. Ablating either the peak token or its preceding governor removes ~all activation, and the output lens promotes no coherent token set (Jacobian kurtosis ~3.0), so it reacts to input already seen rather than preparing a specific upcoming token.
